amount: Living stipend (amount varies by country/circumstances) for up to three years to allow the fellow to work full-time on their idea — Funded; exact figure not standardized, verify current terms on website
other_benefits: Lifetime membership in the global Ashoka Fellows network, connections to co-investors and strategic partners, ongoing organizational and strategic support, access to Ashoka's collaborative entrepreneur community
eligibility: Open to social entrepreneurs in any field (human rights, environment, education, health, economic development, etc.) who have an original systems-changing idea and are leading an initiative to implement it. No degree, age, or nationality restriction; both self-nomination and nomination by others are accepted. Fits graduate students and early-career professionals who are already leading a venture or initiative.
flags: Nomination or self-nomination process (not a standard written application)
notes: One of the original and largest social entrepreneurship fellowship networks (operating since 1981), spanning virtually every field/issue area. No application fee.
duration: Lifetime fellowship designation; direct stipend support typically up to 3 years

name: Halcyon Incubator Fellowship
opens: Twice yearly (spring and fall cohort application cycles; check site for current window)
deadline: Varies by cohort cycle — check current open call on website
amount: $10,000 equity-free stipend, plus in-kind support (e.g., cloud credits, pro bono legal/consulting services)
other_benefits: Five months of rent-free housing and co-working space in residence at Halcyon in Washington, D.C., mentorship and leadership coaching, pro bono legal/business/technical support from partner firms, alumni network access
eligibility: Must be the CEO or primary decision-maker of an early-stage, proof-of-concept-stage social-impact venture (any business sector) with positive social/environmental impact as a core goal; venture can be based anywhere in the world. No specific degree requirement, so open to graduate students and early-career founders.
notes: Residency-based (in-person in Washington, D.C. for 5 months); no fee or equity taken by Halcyon.

name: Link Foundation Energy Fellowship Program
deadline: December 1 (annual; verify exact date each cycle)
amount: $45,000/year for 2 years ($90,000 total) toward academic-year and summer stipend
other_benefits: Two-year renewable PhD support; recognition as a Link Foundation Fellow; no citizenship restriction
eligibility: Open to PhD students (any nationality) in energy-related engineering/science fields, tenable only at U.S. or Canadian universities; preference given to those with a well-defined thesis direction and sufficient time remaining in the program.
notes: Long-running (since 1980s) private foundation fellowship for doctoral energy research; application requires a 500-word research proposal, resume, and three letters of recommendation. No fee found.
location: Not specified (fellow's home PhD-granting institution, U.S. or Canada)

organization: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE) — Solar Energy Technologies Office (SETO)
name: SETO Science, Technology and Policy (STP) Fellowship
other_benefits: Medical/dental/vision insurance supplement, local transportation stipend, one-time $5,000 relocation allowance; placement working with DOE's Solar Energy Technologies Office in Washington, DC
eligibility: Open to those currently pursuing or having completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree in engineering, physical/natural sciences, social science, or a related field, plus established professionals; applicants must be a U.S. citizen or Lawful Permanent Resident.
flags: US citizen/LPR required
notes: Administered through ORISE/Zintellect on behalf of DOE; direct solar background not required. Listing URL is for a recent cycle — check Zintellect catalog for the current open posting each cycle.

name: E4C Fellowship
opens: Annual (application window typically opens ~December, closes mid-February)
deadline: Annual, typically mid-February (2026 cycle closed February 15, 2026 — watch for the next posted cycle)
amount: Stipend for duration of fellowship (amount varies by cost-of-living and expertise, paid in installments tied to milestones); not intended as primary income
other_benefits: Mentorship, professional skill-building, remote/global project team experience, and network within the engineering-for-development field
eligibility: Open to early-career technical professionals — defined as those in their 3rd/4th year of a bachelor's degree, graduate students, or those with fewer than 10 years of relevant professional experience; must be proficient in English and able to commit 20-25 hrs/week remotely.
notes: Focused on engineering for sustainable global development; fellows work part-time (May-September) on an Impact Project with an international team. Requires becoming a free E4C member to apply; no fee found for membership or application.

organization: New Jersey Economic Development Authority (NJEDA) / New Jersey's Clean Energy Program
name: Clean Energy Fellowship Program
amount: Approx. $27,000/year stipend (varies by participating university) plus ~$500/year for travel, materials, and equipment (Rutgers RCEI partner track pays hourly for initial fellowship hours)
other_benefits: Paid independent research placement in a clean-energy sector (solar, wind, geothermal, green hydrogen, fuel cells, biomass, tidal, nuclear, hydropower) with a participating NJ university
eligibility: Open to graduate (master's or doctoral) students — some tracks also include undergraduates — enrolled at a participating New Jersey university (e.g., Rutgers, NJIT, Princeton, Stevens, Rowan, Montclair State, Kean, Seton Hall) conducting clean-energy research.
flags: Limited to NJ-affiliated universities
notes: State-funded program explicitly states no application fees are charged. Administered jointly by NJEDA and partner universities' clean energy institutes (e.g., Rutgers Climate and Energy Institute).
duration: Academic year (renewable across multiple years, e.g., 2026-2027 and 2027-2028)

name: Horowitz Foundation for Social Policy Grant
amount: $7,500 total ($5,000 initial disbursement, $2,500 upon project completion)
other_benefits: Recognition as a Horowitz Fellow; foundation network of past awardees
eligibility: PhD students who have defended their dissertation proposal or had their topic approved by their department; in fields of social policy (sociology, political science, economics, psychology, etc.); US citizenship/residency not required.
notes: Small dissertation-level research grant; non-renewable; five years to complete project and claim final payment.
duration: Up to 5 years to complete project

name: American Sociological Association Minority Fellowship Program (MFP)
deadline: Check ASA site for current-cycle date (historically early winter)
amount: $20,000 annual stipend (August 1-July 31); ASA also works with departments to help cover tuition
other_benefits: Virtual programming, professional development at ASA Annual Meeting, travel support for conferences, mentoring network
eligibility: PhD students enrolled in a sociology doctoral program, advanced in their program, who identify as a member of an underrepresented racial/ethnic group among sociology PhDs (Black/African American, Latino/a/x, American Indian/Alaskan Native, Asian/Pacific Islander, MENA/SWANA).
notes: Applicants typically conduct research with a focus on race, ethnicity, intersectionality, or related topics.
location: Applicant's home institution (program administered by ASA, Washington DC)

name: Russell Sage Foundation Visiting Scholars Program
opens: Applications typically open in the fall/winter preceding the fellowship year
deadline: Late June (annual, e.g. June 25, 2026 for the 2027-2028 cohort)
amount: Full salary replacement/stipend (RSF states support is comparable to visiting scholar's normal academic salary, up to a foundation-set maximum) plus office space; verify exact figures on website
other_benefits: Partially subsidized apartment near RSF's NYC offices for scholars from outside the area; childcare subsidies for children under 13; office space and research support at RSF headquarters
eligibility: Scholars with a PhD or comparable terminal degree (or equivalent career background), at least two years beyond the PhD at the application deadline, proposing research in the social, economic, political, or behavioral sciences.
flags: Residency required (min. 75% of working days in residence at RSF, NYC)
notes: One of the most established residential fellowships specifically for early/mid-career social scientists (post-PhD); 15-17 awarded annually.
location: New York, NY (in-residence at Russell Sage Foundation headquarters)

organization: The Aspen Institute (Aspen Tech Policy Hub)
name: Science & Technology Policy Fellowship
deadline: Annual — typically early February (2026 cycle: Dec 18–Feb 5)
other_benefits: Pairing with experienced policy mentors; access to designers, copy editors, legal experts, and communications specialists to develop a policy proposal; networking dinners with government and corporate policy experts; automatic consideration for the Savilla Pitt Memorial Fellowship
eligibility: Open to science, environment, and technology professionals/experts age 21+, based in the U.S.; a university degree in STEM is not required but candidates with significant prior government policy experience are generally considered too advanced for this introductory program. Priority given to those in emerging technology, cybersecurity, or environment.
notes: Distinct from (and a program of) the Aspen Institute, separate from Aspen's more famous fellowships; focused on training STEM/tech experts to become policy entrepreneurs, culminating in real policy proposals pitched to government/industry.
location: In-residence (historically Bay Area/San Francisco; flexible/hybrid format has been used in some years)

organization: The Foundry (Internet Law & Policy Foundry, ILPF)
name: Foundry Junior Fellowship
opens: Annual — 2026 cohort call opened in spring 2026
deadline: Annual, rolling within cycle — 2026 cohort deadline was June 22, 2026 (early submissions encouraged)
amount: Unpaid/no stipend — Funded — amount not specified; verify on website. Benefit is professional development and network access rather than a stipend.
other_benefits: Complimentary admission to the Foundry's public fee-based events, access to a private professional network and LinkedIn community, participation in Foundry committees (Events, Admissions, Outreach, Content), use of Foundry partners/event spaces/media reach for career development
eligibility: Open globally to students, researchers, legal professionals, policy practitioners, academics, advocates, and technology professionals working at the intersection of law, tech, and policy (including AI, cybersecurity, privacy, internet governance); competitive selection, no fee to apply or participate.
flags: Unpaid — no stipend
notes: Two-year fellowship (Junior Fellow year 1, Senior Fellow year 2) in internet/tech law and policy; a peer-driven professional development community rather than a placement or grant program. No application or membership fee identified for Fellows.
location: Not specified (U.S.-based organization with a global fellow base; hybrid virtual/in-person activities)

name: NXTHVN Studio and Curatorial Fellowship
deadline: Annual (2025-2026 cycle deadline was March 2, 2026; check site for next cycle)
amount: $35,000 stipend for Studio Fellows; $45,000 stipend for Curatorial Fellows (disbursed quarterly)
other_benefits: Studio or office space, subsidized housing, mentorship from established artists and curators, professional development
eligibility: Early-career visual artists and curators selected from an international applicant pool; fellows must relocate to New Haven, CT for the program duration and commit to mentoring a high school apprentice. No application fee found.
flags: Relocation required (New Haven, CT); mentorship commitment required
notes: Up to 7 artists and 2 curators selected per year; founded by artist Titus Kaphar.

name: Sainsbury Management Fellowship
deadline: Rolling; recent windows include 30 Apr 2026, 2 Jun-30 Sep 2026, and 3 Nov 2026-2 Mar 2027
amount: £50,000 toward tuition/costs of a full-time MBA at one of 19 eligible business schools (e.g. Harvard, Stanford, MIT Sloan, Oxford Said, Cambridge Judge, INSEAD)
other_benefits: Access to the Royal Academy of Engineering's Sainsbury Management Fellows network and Engineers and Scientists in Business Fellowship activities; can apply before securing a business school place
eligibility: UK nationals currently living in the UK, holding a first degree in engineering/allied technology/science, generally 4-10 years' post-degree work experience, GMAT of at least 650, and planning/considering a full-time MBA at one of the 19 eligible schools; graduate-level (pre-MBA) applicants explicitly eligible
flags: Restricted to UK nationals; engineering/science first degree required
notes: Long-running scheme (since 1987) funded by the Gatsby Charitable Foundation; over 400 engineers supported to date. No application fee found; contact Programme Manager to register interest.
duration: Length of the full-time MBA program (typically 1-2 years)
location: UK-based applicants; MBA study at partner schools in North America and Europe

organization: The PhD Project / American Marketing Association Academic Council
name: Valuing Diversity PhD Scholarship
other_benefits: Recognition through the AMA Academic Council and The PhD Project network aimed at diversifying business academia
eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents currently enrolled full-time in an AACSB-accredited marketing or advertising doctoral program who have completed at least one year of the program and have not previously received this scholarship
flags: US citizens/permanent residents only; must already be enrolled in a marketing/advertising PhD program
notes: Smaller-dollar award compared to typical 'fellowship' branding (styled as a scholarship) but run in partnership with The PhD Project's long-standing effort to diversify business doctoral education; requires an advisor letter and essay. No application fee found.

name: Educational Testing Service Postdoctoral Fellowship Program (ETS)
opens: Rolling / annual cycle — no formal application form; check ETS Research site for current call
amount: $50,000 stipend annually, plus limited relocation expenses
other_benefits: Mentorship from ETS research staff; access to ETS research infrastructure and data; renewable after year one by mutual agreement
eligibility: Individuals who hold a doctorate in a relevant discipline (psychology, education, measurement, psychometrics, statistics, computer science, linguistics, educational technology, policy research, etc.) with evidence of prior research; program especially encourages women and underrepresented minority applicants
notes: Hosted at ETS headquarters in Princeton, NJ; up to three fellows selected per cycle; goal includes increasing diversity in educational measurement research.

name: Value Assessment and Health Outcomes Research Predoctoral Fellowship
opens: Annual (LOI/application portal opens mid-year via ProposalCentral)
deadline: Annual, typically late October (2025 cycle deadline was October 30)
amount: $30,000/year stipend for 12, 18, or 24 months; up to $1,000/year for research-related incidentals
other_benefits: Supports advanced doctoral training with a focus on patient engagement in health outcomes/value assessment research
eligibility: Doctoral students (U.S. or non-U.S. citizens) enrolled full-time at an accredited U.S. university, having completed at least two years of coursework and engaged in dissertation research; not eligible if holding an NIH F-series award or expecting to graduate before April 1 of the award year; one applicant per research group
notes: Part of PhRMA Foundation's broader predoctoral fellowship program (also offers Drug Discovery, Drug Delivery, and Translational Medicine tracks); applications processed via ProposalCentral

name: American Society of Hematology Scholar Award (Fellow, Fellow-to-Faculty, and Junior Faculty tracks)
deadline: Annual; letter of intent typically due spring, full application around May 1 (check current-cycle dates at hematology.org)
amount: Up to $100,000 (Fellow Scholar), $125,000 (Fellow-to-Faculty), or $150,000 (Junior Faculty) paid over 2-3 years in quarterly installments
other_benefits: Career-transition research support; optional ASH-Peter Steelman Scholar Award track for AML-focused projects with additional funding and scientific summit invitations
eligibility: Holders of MD, MD-PhD, PhD, or PharmD (or equivalent) who are ASH members in good standing, devoting at least 75% full-time effort to research, conducting research in the U.S. or Canada, and not currently holding a substantial prior award (e.g., NIH R01) as PI/co-PI; three career-stage tiers ranging from <6 to 11-13 years post-degree
flags: ASH membership required
notes: One of the longest-running early-career hematology funding programs (since 1985); program significantly expanded funding in 2025-2026

organization: Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research
name: Jane Coffin Childs Postdoctoral Fellowship
deadline: February 1 (annual; portal for the next cycle opens October 1 of the prior year)
amount: Funded — amount not specified; verify on website (stipend-based postdoctoral fellowship in biomedical/cancer research)
other_benefits: Supports independent postdoctoral research training in a new laboratory distinct from the applicant's graduate lab
eligibility: PhD recipients within 24 months of degree conferral (or MD within 3 years), or PhD candidates whose degree will be conferred before the fellowship start date, with no more than 12 months of prior postdoctoral experience at the deadline; citizens of any country eligible, but non-U.S. citizens must train at a U.S. institution; requires a sponsoring lab/institutional commitment; only one Fellow per sponsor's lab funded per award year
flags: Requires sponsoring lab commitment before applying
notes: Long-running fund supporting basic biomedical and cancer research fellows; application portal is closed between cycles (opens October 1 for the following February 1 deadline)
duration: Typically up to 3 years (verify current terms on website)
location: U.S. institutions (non-citizens); any qualifying institution for U.S. citizens

name: Life Sciences Research Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship (LSRF)
opens: Application typically opens in the months before the fall deadline (annual cycle)
deadline: Annual, October 1 (complete application, including reference letters, due by November 1)
amount: Funded — amount not specified; verify on website (multi-year postdoctoral stipend and research support)
other_benefits: Supports independent postdoctoral research training at nonprofit U.S. institutions; part of a competitive national postdoctoral fellowship network
eligibility: Applicants within 5 years of receiving their PhD (or MD/DVM) as of the application deadline; may apply before defending thesis but must hold the degree by fellowship activation; must train in a lab different from their graduate lab, at a nonprofit institution; U.S. citizens may work anywhere, non-U.S. citizens must conduct research at a U.S. laboratory
notes: Broad life-sciences postdoctoral fellowship (biomedical and basic biology research); highly competitive national program
duration: Multi-year postdoctoral fellowship (verify exact term on website)
location: Nonprofit research institutions (U.S. required for non-citizens)

name: American Antiquarian Society Academic Research Fellowships (e.g., Kate B. and Hall J. Peterson Fellowship, Brown Family Collection Fellowship)
amount: Stipend of approximately $1,900-$3,000+ per month depending on specific fellowship (varies by award); no application fee
other_benefits: Access to AAS's world-class collection of pre-1900 American historical and cultural materials; residential support in Worcester, MA
eligibility: Advanced graduate students working on dissertations, postdoctoral scholars, and independent scholars researching American history and culture through 1900; open to international applicants
notes: AAS offers 40+ named fellowships annually across several sub-programs (e.g., Peterson, Jaffee, Brown Family, Lapides); check specific sub-fellowship pages for exact terms

organization: Borchard Foundation Center on Law & Aging
name: Borchard Fellowship in Law and Aging
deadline: April 1 (annual, next cycle TBD — check site for 2027-2029 cycle dates)
other_benefits: Placement with a host organization (law school, government agency, or legal services org) to pursue academic and/or professional work in law and aging; two-year term.
eligibility: Recent law school graduates (JD) interested in pursuing an academic and/or professional career focused on law and aging; no citizenship restriction specified.
notes: Two fellowships awarded per cycle (2-year cohorts, e.g. 2025-2027). Confirm exact next application window on site since cycles run every two years.

organization: University of Michigan, Ross School of Business (Business+Impact)
name: Golub Capital Nonprofit Board Fellows Program
deadline: Unknown — check site for current-cycle deadline after August 2026 opening
amount: Unpaid non-voting board placement; no fellowship stipend identified — verify on website
other_benefits: Placement as a non-voting board member on a local nonprofit board for an academic year; hands-on governance project (~5 hrs/month); can earn the Michigan Ross Nonprofit Governance Endorsement; access to alumni Board Fellows network via Compass Pro Bono
eligibility: Open to current University of Michigan graduate students in any discipline or degree program who will not graduate before April of the participation year; no citizenship restriction identified
flags: Restricted to University of Michigan graduate students
notes: Part of the wider Golub Capital Nonprofit Board Fellows Network (est. 2003 at Kellogg, expanded with a $10M+ Golub Capital gift across multiple business schools). Since 1999 the Michigan program has matched 800+ fellows with 300+ nonprofit boards.
location: Ann Arbor, MI (in-person board service with local nonprofits)

organization: UCLA Anderson School of Management (Center for Impact @ Anderson)
name: Golub Capital UCLA Anderson Board Fellows Program
opens: Unknown — recruitment typically begins in fall for the following calendar year
deadline: Unknown — verify current cycle on website
amount: Unpaid non-voting board placement; no fellowship stipend identified — verify on website
other_benefits: Serves as a non-voting board member with committee involvement; completes a 60+ hour strategic consulting project (board governance, program evaluation, operations, digital/data strategy, or impact measurement) for the partner nonprofit
eligibility: Open to current UCLA Anderson MBA and MSBA (Master of Science in Business Analytics) students; no citizenship restriction identified
flags: Restricted to UCLA Anderson MBA/MSBA students
notes: One of several university programs in the Golub Capital Nonprofit Board Fellows Network; UCLA Anderson's iteration received a dedicated gift from Golub Capital to expand the program.
location: Los Angeles, CA (in-person board service with local nonprofits)

organization: Columbia Business School (Tamer Center for Social Enterprise)
name: Nonprofit Board Leadership Program (NBLP)
opens: Unknown — recruitment occurs at the start of the academic year
deadline: Unknown — verify current cycle on website
amount: Unpaid experiential program; no fellowship stipend identified — verify on website
other_benefits: Student teams (typically pairs) are matched with a nonprofit board (via an alum/friend of the school serving on that board) for a year-long engagement combining board-meeting observation, mentorship, and a student-led consulting project
eligibility: Open to current Columbia Business School students (MBA/graduate students); no citizenship restriction identified
flags: Restricted to Columbia Business School students
notes: Distinct from the Golub Capital network programs but structurally similar; run through Columbia's Tamer Center for Social Enterprise.
location: New York, NY (in-person board engagement with local nonprofits)

organization: Carnegie Mellon University, Tepper School of Business (Accelerate Leadership Center)
name: Golub Capital Board Fellows Program
opens: Early fall semester (applications open at start of first-year MBA fall term)
deadline: Unknown — final fellow selections made in November; verify current-cycle date on website
amount: Unpaid non-voting board placement; no fellowship stipend identified — verify on website
other_benefits: One-to-one match with a nonprofit board as a non-voting member; onboarding sessions and workshops; mentorship; leadership-development programming through the Accelerate Leadership Center
eligibility: Open to first-year Full-Time and Online Hybrid Tepper MBA students in good academic standing who demonstrate interest in nonprofit governance and community impact; no citizenship restriction identified
flags: Restricted to Tepper School (CMU) first-year MBA students; written application plus interview required
notes: Launched its inaugural cohort in 2025 as part of the Golub Capital Nonprofit Board Fellows Network; fellows commit ~2-3 hours/week.
location: Pittsburgh, PA (in-person board service with local nonprofits)

name: Halcyon Fellowship
opens: Rolling/varies by themed cohort (e.g., January 15, 2026 deadline noted for one 2026 cohort)
deadline: Varies by themed fellowship track; check current listings on halcyonhouse.org
amount: Equity-free stipend up to $6,000 per venture, plus up to $10,000 in AWS credits (some themed tracks, e.g. Global Climate Fellowship, offer up to $25,000)
other_benefits: Hybrid virtual + in-person residency program, mentorship, expert advisory support, access to investor network
eligibility: Open to impact-driven, full-time founders (any nationality) who have an MVP and are building a scalable for-profit venture aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals; no formal degree requirement, popular with early-career entrepreneurs
notes: Runs multiple themed cohorts per year (e.g., climate resilience, food security) rather than one fixed annual cycle; verify current open cohort and deadline before applying.
duration: Typically ~6 months per cohort (varies by track)
location: Washington, D.C. (hybrid; virtual + in-person residencies), open globally

name: Rainer Arnhold Fellows Program
opens: Rolling inquiry (recruits year-round; short intake form, no fixed formal application cycle)
deadline: October 31, 2026 (noted intake deadline; program largely recruitment-driven, so check site for current status)
amount: $100,000 funding plus week-long design retreats, coaching, and expert connections
other_benefits: On-ramp to longer-term Mulago Foundation funding, personalized design coaching, peer network of ~20 fellows selected annually from a large applicant pool
eligibility: Open to founders/leaders (any country, any field: health, education, livelihoods, water & sanitation, conservation/climate) of an existing scalable-solution organization; entrepreneurial track record and decision-making authority expected; no specific degree requirement, common among early-career social-sector leaders
flags: Recruitment-driven — apply via short inquiry form rather than lengthy formal application
notes: About 20 new fellows chosen annually out of 1,000+ inquiries; focused on scalable solutions to poverty and conservation, cutting across academic/professional fields.
duration: Not specified (fellowship engagement includes intensive retreat plus ongoing support)
location: Global (foundation based in Northern California, US)

organization: Institute of International Education / Fulbright Program (with Fogarty International Center, NIH)
name: Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health

deadline: Follows standard Fulbright U.S. Student Program deadline (typically early-mid October)
amount: Same benefits as traditional Fulbright Study/Research grants (stipend, travel, and other allowances per host country; exact amount not specified — verify on website)
other_benefits: Placement with NIH-affiliated global health research site; mentorship; cultural/professional exchange experience
eligibility: U.S. citizens who are MD or other professional degree students having completed at least their 3rd year, or PhD candidates who have completed master's-level requirements; enrolled at any accredited U.S. university
flags: U.S. citizens only; limited to specific host countries
notes: Placements currently available in Malaysia, Vietnam, Ghana, Malawi, Uganda, Nepal, Jamaica, and Peru; apply via apply.iie.org/fulbrightusstudent and select this award track
location: Host country abroad (Malaysia, Vietnam, Ghana, Malawi, Uganda, Nepal, Jamaica, or Peru)

name: David A. Winston Health Policy Fellowship

amount: $65,000 annual stipend, plus $2,500 moving expenses and $5,000 for conference fees/travel
other_benefits: Medical and vision insurance covered; monthly Metro transit passes; networking with health policy leaders in public and private sectors
eligibility: Current graduate students (any degree field) in their second semester/third quarter (or next-to-final year for longer programs) at an accredited college or university, graduating within the application cycle (September-June); must be a U.S. citizen
flags: U.S. citizens only; graduate students only (no early-career professionals outside this window)
notes: 12-month paid placement on Capitol Hill, in the Executive Branch, or at healthcare agencies/organizations, beginning in June

organization: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel Center for Advanced Holocaust Studies
name: Summer Graduate Student Research Fellowship

other_benefits: Access to Museum archives, working alongside Mandel Center research staff and scholars in residence
eligibility: Students accepted to or currently enrolled in a master's program, or in the first year of a PhD program, at a college or university in North America.
notes: Focused on Holocaust and genocide studies (history/humanities); requires in-residence research at the Museum in Washington, DC for the fellowship period.

name: Women's Law & Public Policy Fellowship Program (WLPPFP)

eligibility: Open to U.S. law school graduates or students in their final year of law school who are committed to advancing women's rights and public interest law throughout their careers
notes: 12-month fellowship placing fellows with a public interest organization working on women's legal issues, or as a two-year clinical teaching fellow at Georgetown Law. Georgetown also runs a related LAWA (Leadership & Advocacy for Women in Africa) fellowship with a separate January deadline.
duration: 12 months (or 2 years if clinical teaching track)
location: Placement varies; teaching track based in Washington, DC

organization: University of Washington, Foster School of Business / Evans School of Public Policy
name: Board Fellows Program (Consulting and Business Development Center)
opens: Applications reopen annually (2026-27 cycle deadline below); prior cycle opened Sept. 26

other_benefits: Governance bootcamp training, placement as a non-voting board member with a Washington-state nonprofit, committee-level leadership experience, and networking/interview matching events
eligibility: Open to graduate students in their second or third year, including full-time MBA, evening MBA, hybrid MBA, TMMBA, and Evans School MPA students; no citizenship restriction specified
notes: Jointly run by UW Foster's Consulting and Business Development Center and the Evans School of Public Policy; service period runs Jan-June with an extension option.

organization: Dartmouth College, Tuck School of Business — Center for Business, Government & Society

other_benefits: Year-long placement as a non-voting board member with an Upper Valley (NH/VT) nonprofit, applied business/strategy consulting experience, and direct exposure to nonprofit governance practice
eligibility: Open to Tuck MBA candidates (graduate students), with first-year students the primary focus; no citizenship restriction specified
notes: Administered by Tuck's Center for Business, Government & Society; program launch typically in May with academic-year engagement following.

amount: Funded — free to participants; no cash stipend, funding covers matching, training, and support at no cost to Fellows
other_benefits: Matching to a vetted nonprofit board via the BoardLead platform, a BoardLearn governance certification (boot camp), ongoing training/expert access, and a peer network of values-aligned Fellows
eligibility: Open nationally to working professionals — with emphasis on individuals from communities underrepresented on nonprofit boards — committed to nonprofit board service; specific years-of-experience thresholds have varied by cohort, so early-career applicants should confirm current-cycle criteria directly with the program
flags: Verify current cohort's experience-level eligibility bar before applying
notes: Entirely free program per the organization's own materials ("all of these opportunities entirely FREE of cost"); applications are processed through the BoardLead platform rather than a standalone form.
duration: Roughly 4-5 months per cohort (e.g., January launch to May board elections)
location: United States (nationwide; virtual info sessions and convenings)

organization: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
name: P.D. Soros Fellowship for New Americans
deadline: October 29, 2026, 2:00 PM ET (for the 2027 fellowship class)

other_benefits: Placement with a host organization in Michigan's transportation/mobility ecosystem, hands-on project work, professional mentorship and network-building across the state's mobility sector
eligibility: Recent graduates (within two years of any degree) from across the US; early-career professionals interested in transportation and mobility
flags: Placement and program activity centered in Michigan; relocation likely required

name: Loeb Fellowship

notes: A highly selective, long-running (est. 1970) one-year fellowship at Harvard GSD for accomplished practitioners in urban planning and related built-environment fields to step back, study, and reflect. Best fit for early-to-mid-career professionals nearing the upper end of F4F's target range; verify current eligibility language on the official site.
duration: One academic year (mid-August through commencement, roughly 9-10 months)
location: Cambridge, Massachusetts (Harvard GSD campus; in-residence required)

name: Abel Wolman Fellowship

other_benefits: Potential for AWWA conference networking and recognition; renewable second-year funding for continuing PhD research
eligibility: PhD students in the U.S., Canada, or Mexico who are at most two years from completing their doctoral program in water supply and treatment-related fields; three recommendation letters required, including one from the dissertation advisor

flags: PhD-track students only, must be within final two years of degree
notes: AWWA's flagship doctoral fellowship supporting advanced water supply and treatment research; administered through AWWA's centralized scholarship application portal alongside its other water-focused scholarships.

flags: Requires a permanent, independent position; postdocs not eligible (targets faculty/independent researchers within 10 years of degree, not current grad students)
notes: Part of the National Academies' Gulf Research Program, focused on Gulf of Mexico region human health, energy, and environmental resilience; the Environment Track directly funds natural resource stewardship research for early-career independent investigators.

location: Not specified (home institution-based, U.S. Gulf-region relevance)

eligibility: Graduate students or recent graduates (within two years of degree completion, or within one year of completing a graduate degree) with strong interest and experience in coastal/natural resource policy; preference given to Oregon-based institution applicants but open to applicants from any U.S. university

organization: Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health (ASPPH), in partnership with USDA

other_benefits: Placement at USDA Rural Development in Washington, DC (hybrid/remote candidates considered); possible one-year extension; mentorship and hands-on rural health policy experience
eligibility: Must hold a Master's or Doctorate degree (received within roughly the last 5 years) from an ASPPH member school/program of public health accredited by CEPH; must be a US citizen or hold a Green Card
flags: US citizens or Green Card holders only; must be a graduate of an ASPPH member/CEPH-accredited public health program
notes: A full-time, one-year paid training fellowship placing a recent public health graduate directly inside USDA's Rural Development office to work on rural health initiatives with federal and non-federal partners. Recurs annually; verify current-cycle dates and dollar amounts on ASPPH's site since older program announcements (2023) were the most complete source found.
duration: One year (est. June-to-June), with possible one-year extension

name: National Rural Health Association Rural Health Fellows Leadership Program (NRHA)

amount: Not specified; verify on website (program is training-based, not a stipend program)
other_benefits: Year-long leadership training with three in-person sessions and monthly virtual meetings; development of a policy brief that may inform NRHA's national advocacy; limited financial support available for fellows who need it via a program sponsor
eligibility: Early-to-mid career professionals with demonstrated commitment to rural health; must be an NRHA member for at least one year prior to applying and maintain membership throughout; must be able to attend all in-person sessions
flags: Requires NRHA membership (paid) for at least a year prior; travel/accommodation costs are largely the fellow's or their employer's responsibility (limited sponsor support available)
notes: A widely recognized rural health leadership-training fellowship (over 200 alumni) aimed at early- and mid-career professionals, not just students; selects roughly 15-20 fellows per year. Best fit for early-career professionals already working in rural health/community development rather than current students.
location: Hybrid: monthly virtual sessions plus three in-person training sessions (US)

name: Farm Foundation Agricultural Economics Fellow Program

notes: A yearlong, in-residence fellowship for an early-career agricultural economist to work on rural and agricultural policy issues (e.g., the 2025 fellow focused on bioeconomy). Runs as a small annual cohort (one fellow), separate from Farm Foundation's broader Roundtable/graduate-scholar programs.
location: Not specified (Farm Foundation is based in Illinois; some remote/hybrid work likely)

organization: Northern Michigan University, in partnership with InvestUP

flags: Restricted to NMU's own enrolled MPA/MBA graduate students -- not open to the general public or students at other institutions
notes: A state-backed (Michigan Economic Development Corporation-funded) rural capacity-building fellowship pairing NMU graduate students with rural Upper Peninsula community development projects; funds full tuition plus a living stipend for one academic year.

organization: Carter G. Woodson Institute for African American and African Studies, University of Virginia

flags: Must relocate to and reside full-time in Charlottesville, VA
notes: Long-running annual postdoctoral research fellowship at one of the oldest African American studies research centers in the U.S.; next cycle (for appointment beginning July 2027) has letters of recommendation due December 8, 2026.

organization: Carter G. Woodson Institute for African American and African Studies, University of Virginia

eligibility: PhD candidates who are ABD (all requirements completed except dissertation) working on African American and African Diasporic Studies topics; international students eligible; preference to those with substantially completed research
flags: Must relocate to and reside full-time in Charlottesville, VA for the fellowship term
notes: Two-year residential dissertation-completion fellowship; a strong option for advanced PhD students finishing dissertations in African American/African diasporic topics.

organization: Hutchins Center for African & African American Research, Harvard University

eligibility: Pre-doctoral (dissertation-stage) and post-doctoral scholars conducting individual research related to African and African American Studies; specific categories have their own eligibility criteria
flags: Verify current-cycle deadline directly on website, as it changes annually

duration: One to two semesters (varies by fellowship category)

organization: Dartmouth College, Department of Latin American, Latino, and Caribbean Studies

other_benefits: Research expense allocation, mentoring and professional development programming, faculty career preparation guidance, support through the Guarini School for Graduate and Advanced Studies, community initiative access
eligibility: ABD graduate students (any discipline) whose dissertation addresses the interdisciplinary field of Latinx Studies/Latinx experience and culture
flags: 2026-28 cycle closed; watch for next annual posting
notes: Two-year residential predoctoral-to-postdoctoral fellowship at Dartmouth; fellow teaches one course in year two and joins the Provost's Fellowship Program cohort. Dartmouth also runs a closely related César Chávez Dissertation and Postdoctoral Fellowship on the same model.

organization: UC Berkeley Center for Latin American and Caribbean Studies / U.S. Department of Education (Title VI)
name: Foreign Language and Area Studies (FLAS) Fellowship - Latin American Studies
amount: Language program fees up to $5,000 plus a stipend (reported at $3,500 for the summer track); academic-year FLAS awards are typically larger and vary by institution
other_benefits: Funds a full academic year or intensive summer of language instruction; study may occur at UC Berkeley, another U.S. university, or an approved foreign university
eligibility: U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents accepted for or currently enrolled in a graduate program; preference to students combining language study with area/international studies focused on Latin America
flags: US citizens/nationals/permanent residents only; funding availability for Latin American languages varies by year
notes: FLAS is a national U.S. Department of Education Title VI program administered independently by dozens of university-based Latin American studies centers; Berkeley's cycle is used here as one representative, currently-open implementation. Applicants should also check FLAS pages at other Title VI centers (e.g., UF, UT-Austin, Columbia, UCLA) since deadlines and awards vary by host institution.
duration: Minimum 6-week intensive program (summer) or full academic year, depending on track
location: UC Berkeley or approved partner institution

organization: University of Arizona Center for Latin American Studies / Tinker Foundation
name: Tinker Field Research Grant (Tinker Field Research Collaborative)
other_benefits: Covers travel and limited field research expenses in Latin America and the Caribbean; supports pilot studies, language/cultural immersion, and scholarly network development
eligibility: Graduate students in any discipline at University of Arizona (or other Tinker Field Research Collaborative member institutions) conducting master's thesis or pre-dissertation fieldwork in Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking Latin American countries; must show language proficiency and plan at least 21 full-time research days (max four months)
flags: Only open to students at Tinker Field Research Collaborative member universities (about 15 institutions, including Arizona, Berkeley, NYU, Kansas); apply through your home institution's Latin American studies center, not directly to the Tinker Foundation
notes: Long-running Tinker Foundation program (since 1979) now delivered through a consortium of ~15 university Latin American studies centers rather than direct national application; University of Arizona's cycle is used here as a representative, currently-open example. Students should check whether their own university is a Collaborative member for locally-administered deadlines.
duration: Up to four months of fieldwork (minimum 21 full-time research days)
location: 19 eligible Latin American/Caribbean countries (fieldwork abroad; grant administered from U.S. host university)

name: Japanese Studies Fellowship Program (Doctoral Candidates Category)
opens: Not specified (2026-2027 cycle guidelines released ahead of a December 1 deadline; info session held October 2025)
deadline: December 1, 2025, 11:59pm EST (for 2026-2027 fellowship period beginning June 2026-March 2027); next cycle expected annually around December 1
amount: Not specified; covers airfare, health insurance, settling-in/departure allowances, monthly stipend, dependent allowance, and enrollment fees (exact stipend amount varies and is not publicly listed)
other_benefits: Airfare, health insurance, settling-in and departure allowances, monthly stipend, dependent allowance and insurance, and enrollment fees where applicable
eligibility: Doctoral candidates in the humanities or social sciences who have achieved ABD (All But Dissertation) status by the fellowship start date, need to conduct research in Japan to complete their dissertation, have sufficient Japanese proficiency, and are US citizens or permanent residents
flags: US citizens/permanent residents only (New York office program); requires ABD status and Japanese-language proficiency
notes: Administered by the Japan Foundation, New York office for US-based applicants. Part of a broader Japanese Studies Fellowship Program that also includes Long-Term and Short-Term categories for scholars with a PhD; only the Doctoral category applies to graduate students. Fellowship duration is 4-12 months.

name: Korea Foundation Scholarship for Graduate Studies (GS)
opens: Varies by world region (e.g., North America group application window typically January-February)

amount: Tuition support (amount varies by region/country cost of living and local tuition levels); not a fixed published dollar figure
other_benefits: Support intended to cover tuition; approximately 150 awards made annually worldwide across all KF scholarship categories
eligibility: Non-Korean citizens (or Korean citizens with permanent residency abroad) currently enrolled or about to enroll full-time in an MA or PhD program in Korean studies or a Korea-related research topic outside Korea; natural science, medicine, engineering, MBA, law, and translation/interpretation students are not eligible; preference given to applicants proficient in Korean
flags: Not open to Korean citizens residing in Korea; ineligible fields (STEM, MBA, law, translation) excluded; cannot hold concurrent fellowships from KF or other institutions
notes: Master's candidates may receive up to 2 years of funding; doctoral candidates up to 3 years, though each award cycle covers one year at a time. Recipients must submit their completed thesis/dissertation to KF upon degree completion.

location: Not specified (grantee's home university, outside Korea)

name: Fulbright-Hays Doctoral Dissertation Research Abroad (DDRA) Fellowship
opens: Not specified (Notice Inviting Applications is announced without advance warning each cycle, typically in fall/early winter)
deadline: Not specified for the 2026-2027 cycle at time of research (recent cycles have closed in January; deadline window is historically 36-77 days after the Notice Inviting Applications is published -- check iris.ed.gov for the current Federal Register notice)

other_benefits: Covers international travel, a maintenance allowance based on host-country cost of living, research expenses, and health insurance for 6-12 months of dissertation research abroad
eligibility: US citizens, nationals, or permanent residents who are PhD candidates admitted to candidacy in a doctoral program in modern foreign languages and area studies, planning a teaching career in the US, with adequate language skills for the dissertation project; applications are submitted through the student's home university, not directly by the student

flags: US citizens/nationals/permanent residents only; federal program subject to annual appropriations and administrative changes -- confirm current-cycle status directly with the Department of Education before relying on it
notes: Not exclusively an Asia-focused program -- it funds dissertation fieldwork across several world regions (Africa, Central/Eastern Europe and Eurasia, Near East, Western Hemisphere excluding the US) but explicitly includes East Asia, Southeast Asia/Pacific, and South Asia as eligible focus areas, making it a major funding source for Asian Studies dissertation research. Apply through your university's Fulbright-Hays coordinator/graduate school, not individually.
duration: 6 to 12 months of full-time dissertation research abroad
location: Host country/countries in the applicant's Asian Studies research region

eligibility: Dissertation-level graduate students and scholars with a special interest in China, Taiwan, or Inner Asia; applicants must be current AAS members (note: AAS membership dues apply, though this is a professional-association membership fee, not an application fee)
area: China / Inner Asia Studies / Asian Studies
flags: Requires current AAS membership to apply
notes: Formerly known as the China and Inner Asia Council (CIAC) Small Grants. A smaller, targeted grant well-suited to dissertation-stage graduate students needing modest project or travel funding for China, Taiwan, or Inner Asia-focused research. Contact grants@asianstudies.org with questions.
duration: Not specified (single project/travel grant, not a multi-year award)

organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison, Center for Research on Gender and Women / Department of Gender & Women's Studies
name: Kaplan Dissertation Fellowship in LGBTQ+ Studies

Segregated/special fees remain the recipient's responsibility even though tuition is remitted.

eligibility: Graduate students at any stage of dissertation work conducting research on contemporary LGBTQIA+ issues aimed at reducing stigma, prejudice, and discrimination; open to applicants of diverse ages, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities, and geographic locations

Not limited to psychology PhD students specifically but research must relate to LGBTQIA+ issues. Requires dissertation abstract, statement of need, and CV via GivingData portal.

eligibility: PhD completed after September 1, 2021 (or equivalent by start date), social science perspective on sexuality studies; must affiliate with Gender & Sexuality Studies plus one partner department (e.g., Anthropology, Black Studies, Communication, History, Political Science, Sociology, etc.); must be available in-residence for the full two-year term

organization: Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society, Harvard University
name: Berkman Klein Center Fellowship

other_benefits: Shared office space at Harvard Law School, access to Harvard libraries and research facilities, health insurance eligibility, opportunity to audit Harvard courses and pursue teaching opportunities, visa sponsorship for international applicants

flags: Recent cycles have prioritized AI-governance research; residency in Cambridge, MA is strongly encouraged though non-resident fellowships are considered case-by-case
notes: One of the most prominent interdisciplinary fellowships covering the intersection of internet governance, disinformation, elections, and political communication in digital spaces. The Center runs an annual competitive cycle; check the fellowships page directly for the next open call since this is a rolling/annual program currently between cycles.

location: Cambridge, MA (Harvard Law School campus); non-resident arrangements considered case-by-case

eligibility: Nationals of an African country, age 35 or under, holding a degree in architecture, urban design, landscape architecture, engineering, or a related built-environment field; must be able to relocate to Kigali, Rwanda for the fellowship term
