amount: $1,000 stipend to attend and read at the annual ALTA conference
other_benefits: Featured public reading at the conference; networking with the literary translation community
eligibility: Open to individual 'emerging translators' (no book-length translation yet published or under contract) of any age/career stage, including current or prospective graduate students in translation, comparative literature, or MFA programs. One fellow is preferentially designated the Peter K. Jansen Memorial Travel Fellow: an emerging translator of color or one working from an underrepresented diaspora/stateless language — same application, no separate form.
flags: Translators only, not co-translator teams
notes: Funds travel to and a featured reading at the ALTA annual conference (ALTA49 is in Portland, OR, Oct 21-24, 2026). No application fee.
duration: One-time award tied to conference attendance
location: Conference location varies by year (2026: Portland, OR)

organization: Black Rock Press, School of the Arts, University of Nevada, Reno
name: Black Rock Press Fellowship (Redfield Fellowship)
deadline: Rolling/varies by cycle; check site (posted periodically alongside MFA admissions, roughly every 2 years)
amount: Not specified (funded 2-year graduate position: full-time work, studio/press access, and support to continue independent artistic practice)
other_benefits: Access to Black Rock Press facilities and equipment
eligibility: A 2-year graduate fellowship for an emerging artist enrolled in book arts, publication arts, or printmaking (typically paired with UNR's MFA program) to work within Black Rock Press's academic and publishing operations.
flags: Tied to UNR MFA program
notes: Combines coursework/practice with hands-on fine-press printing, letterpress, typography, and bookmaking experience.

name: Book Art Research Fellowship
other_benefits: Access to Center for Book Arts' book-art collection
eligibility: Open to researchers and scholars, including current graduate students, in art history, literature, book history, library science, museum studies, conservation studies, or related fields.
notes: 2-3 weeks of on-site research using Center for Book Arts' collections; no application fee.

organization: Smithsonian American Art Museum / Terra Foundation for American Art
name: Terra Foundation Fellowships in American Art (Summer Graduate Fellowship)
deadline: October 15, annual (via Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program application)
amount: $8,000 stipend for a 10-week summer term, plus possible relocation allowance
other_benefits: Mentorship from SAAM curatorial/research staff
eligibility: Open to MA and PhD students who have not yet advanced to candidacy; especially encourages applicants from groups historically underrepresented in American art scholarship (people of color, Indigenous, disabled, LGBTQ+, first-gen, low-income, veteran).
notes: Residential fellowship supporting independent research in Smithsonian American Art Museum collections; apply via the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program (SIFP) portal, proposing a SAAM advisor.
location: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, DC

name: Curator's Fellowship
deadline: Early February, annual (2026 cycle closed Feb 6, 2026; next cycle ~Jan-Feb 2027)
other_benefits: Public presentation opportunity; access to MOHAI collections
eligibility: Open to community and academic researchers/historians, including graduate students (e.g., past fellows pursuing a Museology MA), researching Pacific Northwest history using MOHAI's collections.
notes: 6-month project with 10-20 hours of on-site research; priority given to research centering historically marginalized/excluded communities (Black, Indigenous, POC).

name: McReynolds Curatorial Fellowship (NTX Graduate Student Program)
deadline: Early September, annual (2025 cycle closed Sept 8, 2025; next cycle ~Sept 2026)
amount: Paid academic-year fellowship (specific stipend not disclosed publicly)
other_benefits: Direct curatorial mentorship and exhibition-organizing experience
eligibility: Open to North Texas graduate students pursuing a Master's in Art History with a thesis focused on contemporary art, at any point in their academic journey.
flags: North Texas graduate students
notes: Fellow assists in organizing the MFA student exhibition and supports the Dallas Contemporary curatorial team's research. No application fee.

organization: Arizona State University & Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
name: ASU-LACMA Master's Fellowship in Art History
deadline: January, annual (varies; check site for current-year date)
amount: Fully funded 3-year Master's degree (tuition covered) while continuing museum employment/salary
other_benefits: Structured curatorial mentorship and career-track development toward museum leadership
eligibility: For museum staff (minimum 1 year employed) at ASU-LACMA partner institutions who want to earn a fully funded MA in Art History at ASU while working — a funded pathway into graduate study for museum professionals, designed to diversify museum curatorial staff and leadership.
flags: Requires prior museum employment at a partner institution
notes: Requires current employment at a participating partner museum; the fellowship itself funds entry into and completion of the graduate degree.
location: Arizona State University / partner museums nationally

organization: Smithsonian American Art Museum & National Museum of the American Indian
name: Betsy James Wyeth Fellowship in Native American Art (Predoctoral track)
deadline: October 15, annual (2025 cycle closed; next cycle ~October 2026)
amount: $53,000 stipend (12-month predoctoral residency) plus up to $5,000 for short research trips
other_benefits: Health insurance support and travel funding to Washington, DC
eligibility: Predoctoral track requires completed coursework and preliminary exams, with the candidate actively engaged in dissertation research on historic or contemporary Native American artists, designers, or makers, applying Indigenous methodologies.
notes: Joint SAAM/NMAI fellowship; also has postdoctoral/senior tracks (not grad-eligible) — only the predoctoral track applies here.

name: MFA Fellowships in Painting and Sculpture
deadline: Nomination deadline mid-December; application deadline January 15, annual (2026 cycle: Jan 15, 2026)
other_benefits: Recognition from a jury of distinguished artists, curators, and critics
eligibility: Open to final-year MFA students in Painting or Sculpture graduating from a U.S. program; U.S. citizenship not required. Candidates must be nominated by their MFA department chairperson (each institution may nominate up to two students) — a current-graduate-student-only fellowship.
flags: Nomination-based, not direct self-apply
notes: No self-application; work through your MFA program chair for nomination. No application fee.

organization: Council for the Advancement of Science Writing (CASW)
name: Taylor/Blakeslee Graduate Fellowships
deadline: Mid-March annually (2026 cycle deadline was March 16, 2026; next cycle expected ~March 2027)
amount: $6,000 per fellow (funded by The Brinson Foundation)
eligibility: Students entering or enrolled in a U.S. graduate-level science-writing program (master's programs such as MIT, UC Santa Cruz, NYU SHERP, etc.); explicitly for current/incoming graduate students in science journalism.
notes: Seven fellowships awarded annually. Application via CASW's Submittable portal (casw.submittable.com). No fee.

organization: UC Santa Cruz Science Communication Program
name: Astrobiology Science Communication Graduate Fellowship
deadline: Priority review by January 9 annually (funding tied to UCSC Science Communication Program admission cycle)
eligibility: Admitted/incoming graduate students in UCSC's Science Communication Program (a one-year science journalism master's-equivalent certificate) who focus their capstone project on astrobiology; must submit a 500-word essay on astrobiology interests.
notes: One of several named fellowships listed on this page for UCSC Science Communication Program students; chosen here as the most distinct/obscure of the set.

name: Michael I. Arnolt Center for Investigative Journalism Fellowship
deadline: Not specified (tied to general M.S. Journalism admissions deadline)
amount: Annual financial support (full or partial) plus health, dental, and life insurance; exact stipend not published
other_benefits: Health, dental, and life insurance coverage
eligibility: Students admitted to Indiana University's M.S. in Journalism (investigative concentration); fellows spend roughly a third of the two-year program working in the Arnolt Center, earning 9-12 credit hours as a fellow.
notes: Contact The Media School graduate admissions or arnoltcenter.org for exact current-cycle deadline/stipend figures.

name: Bridging Investigative Journalism (BRIJ) Fellowship
deadline: Not specified (announced annually to enrolled MA Journalism & Public Affairs students)
amount: No cash stipend; fully covers round-trip airfare, and three weeks' room and board in Bergen, Norway
other_benefits: International investigative-reporting exchange with University of Bergen (SUJO)
eligibility: Open only to enrolled students in American University's MA in Journalism & Public Affairs program; up to 5 students selected annually.
notes: Exchange partnership with University of Bergen's Center for Investigative Journalism (SUJO); AU students host Bergen students in DC for 3 weeks, then travel to Norway for 3 weeks.

name: Investigative Reporting Workshop Graduate Fellow
deadline: Not specified; tied to SOC graduate fellowship/scholarship cycle
amount: Not specified (graduate fellowship position; contact SOC for stipend/tuition details)
eligibility: Open to American University School of Communication graduate students; fellow researches and reports for a major investigation during the academic year alongside partners like The Washington Post, Tampa Bay Times, WAMU, and WWNO.

name: Doctoral Fellowship Program (Teaching / Synor / RJI tracks)
amount: $31,200-$33,500 annual stipend (varies by track), full tuition waiver, health insurance, up to $5,000/year for research/conference travel
eligibility: Applicants to Missouri's PhD in Journalism/Strategic Communication; the Doctoral Teaching Fellowship and Synor Doctoral Fellowship favor candidates with professional experience and a master's degree; the RJI Doctoral Fellowship requires substantial professional experience and work with the Reynolds Journalism Institute research director.
notes: Three parallel doctoral fellowship tracks at one school; listed as a single umbrella entry.

organization: University of Chicago (Data Science Institute / Mansueto Institute)
name: Data Science Journalism Fellowship (Local Data Journalism Initiative)
deadline: Rolling within each cycle; check current posting
eligibility: University of Chicago graduate students and advanced undergraduates with math/CS/data-science backgrounds; explicitly open to graduate students.
notes: Pairs data-science fellows with journalist partners to support investigative reporting.

organization: Walter Cronkite School of Journalism (ASU) / Indigenous Journalists Association / ICT
name: ICT/IJA Graduate Fellowship
amount: $26,544 academic-year salary (biweekly, Aug-May) plus tuition covered for all three semesters and health insurance
other_benefits: 15-hour/week paid internship at ICT; IJA convention travel covered
eligibility: IJA members with a bachelor's degree, accepted into a Cronkite master's program (Investigative Journalism, Sports Journalism, Mass Communication, or Strategic Communication) starting Fall 2026 on the Downtown Phoenix campus; explicitly a graduate fellowship.
notes: Fellows work 15 hrs/week for ICT and 5 hrs/week for Cronkite; travel/participation costs for the annual IJA convention included.

organization: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
name: Global Health Reporting Fellowship
deadline: Mid-April annually (2026 cycle deadline was April 14, 2026); check for next cycle
amount: Not specified (single fellow selected per year)
eligibility: Explicitly open to any Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health degree student (including students graduating that May).
notes: Only one fellow chosen per year.

organization: WGBH / American Archive of Public Broadcasting (funded by Institute of Museum and Library Services)
name: Public Broadcasting Preservation Fellowship
opens: Cohorts run spring (Jan-Apr) and summer (Jun-Aug) annually
deadline: Not specified; check host-site pages for current cycle
amount: Not specified (paid fellowship; funded by IMLS)
eligibility: Graduate students in library/information science or archival science programs at five partner universities: UNC Chapel Hill, University of Missouri, University of Oklahoma, Clayton State University, and San Jose State University, each paired with a local public media station.
notes: Fellows inventory, digitize, and catalog public-media audiovisual collections and generate preservation metadata; 10 fellowships total across both terms.

name: Fulcrum Journalism Fellowship (Fall cohort)
deadline: August 3, 2026 (Fall 2026 cohort); program also runs a summer cohort with a separate deadline
eligibility: Explicitly open to undergraduate AND graduate journalism students nationwide in good academic standing.
notes: 10-week solutions-journalism training program (Fall cohort runs Sept 14-Oct 20, 2026); apply via email to newsroom@fulcrum.us. No fee.

organization: Stanford University (Stanford Medicine, Center for Innovation in Global Health)
name: Global Health Media Fellowship
deadline: January 19 annually (2026-27 cycle deadline was Jan 19, 2026); next cycle ~Dec 2026-Jan 2027
amount: Stipend from CNN during the internship portion, plus modest travel allowance
eligibility: Explicitly limited to current allopathic (MD) or osteopathic (DO) medical students at U.S. medical institutions (not open to residents; 4th-years may delay residency a year to participate); need not attend Stanford.
notes: Up to 12-month program: fall coursework at Stanford's journalism program, winter internship at CNN Atlanta, spring capstone project.

organization: National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ) / Northwestern Medill
name: Reuters-NABJ Fellowship
opens: Rolling with Medill graduate admissions (summer-quarter start)
deadline: Tied to Medill's graduate admissions deadline for the summer quarter start
amount: $40,000 scholarship toward tuition, plus a 3-month paid summer internship at Reuters in New York
eligibility: Applicants must be admitted to and enroll in Medill's graduate journalism program (summer quarter start) and be a member of NABJ; explicitly a graduate-student fellowship.
notes: Includes mentorship from Reuters editors during the fellowship year.

name: University Film and Video Association Graduate Student Fellowship (UFVA)
deadline: Varies annually (typically prior to the annual UFVA conference each summer) - check ufva.org for current cycle
amount: Conference travel/registration stipend (exact amount varies by year; not published)
other_benefits: Professional-development Fellows Program (job-market preparation)
eligibility: Explicitly open to graduate students in film, video, and media production programs.
notes: Selected fellows attend the annual UFVA conference and join a year-long professional-development Fellows Program aimed at positioning graduate students for academic/industry jobs; includes documentary and non-fiction film production students.

name: Amazon Lab126 Diversity in Robotics and AI PhD Fellowship
deadline: Not publicly posted — contact the Maryland Robotics Center
amount: Merit-based fellowship (stipend/tuition support; amount not publicly disclosed); recipients may be invited to a paid Lab126 summer internship
eligibility: Current or incoming PhD students in robotics/AI at the University of Maryland (mobile robotics, motion planning, computer vision, pedestrian tracking, ML); two or more awarded per year
flags: No publicly posted amount/deadline/apply-link — verify directly with UMD before listing as fully self-serve.
notes: University-internal program administered by the Maryland Robotics Center rather than a general open call; no public application portal found, so applicants should email the Center directly to ask about the current cycle.
location: University of Maryland, College Park, MD

name: American Welding Society Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship (AWS)
amount: $35,000/year, renewable up to 3 years (paid in two $17,500 installments)
eligibility: Master's or PhD students conducting welding/joining-related research at a North American university under a sponsoring professor; requires free AWS student membership
notes: Must publish in the Welding Journal Research Supplement and present at a future FABTECH conference; cannot combine with an AWS scholarship in the same year.

organization: Embassy of France in the United States / Office for Science and Technology
name: Chateaubriand Fellowship — STEM Track
amount: Monthly stipend up to €1,850, plus round-trip airfare to France and health insurance, for a 4-9 month research stay
eligibility: PhD students enrolled at a US university (any citizenship except French) conducting STEM or health research, to spend part of their dissertation research co-supervised in a French lab
notes: Research-mobility fellowship, not a full degree fellowship; requires a French host lab and a letter of agreement from both US and French advisors.
location: France (fellow relocates from a US PhD program)

name: Link Foundation Modeling, Simulation & Training Fellowship
eligibility: PhD students at any accredited university conducting modeling, simulation, or (especially) human-in-the-loop training research
notes: One of three distinct Link Foundation PhD fellowships (see also Ocean Engineering and Energy, below).
location: USA (open to accredited university PhD students)

name: 3M Science & Technology Graduate Fellowship
deadline: Set by each department's internal nomination deadline — no public direct-apply date
amount: Year 1: $25,000 stipend + tuition (up to 14 credits/semester) + subsidized health insurance; Years 2-4: $8,000/year supplementing a 50% departmental assistantship
eligibility: Incoming PhD students in science or engineering fields aligned with 3M's priority research areas at the University of Minnesota, regardless of citizenship (preference to US citizens/permanent residents)
flags: Not a direct-apply program — nomination required through the department; note this clearly for users.
notes: Nomination-only — students cannot apply directly; must be nominated by their department's Director of Graduate Studies or Graduate Program Coordinator.
location: University of Minnesota, Minneapolis/St. Paul, MN

organization: US Department of Energy, Office of Nuclear Energy / Idaho National Laboratory
name: Nuclear Energy University Program (NEUP) — University Nuclear Leadership Program (UNLP) Graduate Fellowship
amount: $175,000 total over 3 years (stipend, tuition, and a DOE national laboratory summer internship)
eligibility: First- or second-year graduate students (MS/PhD) in nuclear science, nuclear engineering, or related fields at a US institution; students may apply regardless of whether their institution is yet UNLP-approved (approval needed before funds transfer)
notes: Substantial 3-year award; no professional-society membership required to apply.

organization: American Chemical Society, Division of Analytical Chemistry
name: American Chemical Society Division of Analytical Chemistry Graduate Fellowships (ACS)
amount: Four fellowships: Agilent/ACS and Eli Lilly/ACS at $27,000 (9 months) each; Eastman/ACS and Pittcon/ACS at $9,000 (3 months) each
eligibility: Full-time PhD students who have completed at least two years of graduate study, with analytical chemistry central to their dissertation; the applicant's research supervisor (not the applicant) must be an ACS Division of Analytical Chemistry member; three letters of recommendation required, one from the advisor
notes: Discipline-society graduate fellowship; the membership requirement falls on the faculty research supervisor rather than the student applicant, so it does not trigger the applicant-fee exclusion.

name: Barbara L. Jackson Scholars Network
opens: Nominations solicited annually; contact jsn@ucea.org for current cycle
amount: No direct cash stipend to the scholar; nominating institution commits at least $2,000/year per scholar to cover conference registration, travel, lodging, and meals
eligibility: Current doctoral students of color in educational leadership/administration PhD or EdD programs at a UCEA member institution, nominated (no self-nominations) by their dean or Plenum Session Representative, intending to become professors of educational leadership
flags: Nomination-required, not self-apply; no direct cash stipend
notes: Two-year formal mentoring, networking, and professional-development program; scholars attend two UCEA Conventions and two AERA Annual Meetings with institution-paid travel. Nomination-only, not a self-application process.

organization: Center on History and Education, Teachers College, Columbia University
name: Center on History and Education Dissertation Fellowship (CHE)
deadline: Not specified on program page; contact CHE directly
eligibility: Current Teachers College, Columbia University doctoral (PhD/EdD) students whose dissertation focuses in whole or in part on the history of education, in any place or time period
flags: Institution-restricted to Teachers College doctoral students
notes: Restricted to Teachers College students; not open to applicants from other institutions.

organization: Wisconsin Center for Education Research, University of Wisconsin–Madison (IES-funded)
name: Interdisciplinary Training Program for Predoctoral Research in the Education Sciences (ITP)
opens: Tied to admission cycle of partner PhD departments; check site for current recruitment
deadline: Not specified on program page; contact program directly
amount: Full tuition and benefits, stipend, and a small research/travel fund (IES grant covers up to 3 of 5 years; university funds remaining years)
other_benefits: Housed within the Wisconsin Center for Education Research; interdisciplinary coursework plus field-based research training
eligibility: PhD students admitted to a partner UW–Madison doctoral program (sociology, economics, psychology, political science, social welfare, educational leadership and policy analysis, educational policy studies, or educational psychology) who apply concurrently to the ITP
notes: IES Predoctoral Interdisciplinary Research Training Program; recruits roughly 22 doctoral fellows over the grant period.
duration: 5-year fellowship; current grant runs through June 30, 2027

organization: SPARC Consortium: NC State, Texas A&M, Florida State, George Mason, UCF, UNC Charlotte (OSEP-funded)
name: SPARC Consortium Doctoral Fellowship
opens: Varies by partner university's doctoral admissions cycle
deadline: Not specified; check each partner institution
amount: Full financial support (tuition, stipend) under an OSEP Doctoral Training Grant; consortium will fund 22 scholars total
eligibility: Doctoral (PhD) students in special education at one of the six consortium universities who want to become special education teacher-education leaders
notes: Office of Special Education Programs (OSEP) Research to Practice 325H Doctoral Training Grant; scholars develop expertise in teaching, research, policy/advocacy, and research-to-practice partnerships.
duration: Multi-year, tied to doctoral program length; recipients owe 2 years of field service per year of funding

organization: University of Maryland and Vanderbilt University (OSEP-funded)
name: Project SUSTAIN
opens: Annual cycle; most recent cohort applications due December 1
deadline: December 1 (verify current-year date with UMD Special Education PhD program)
amount: Full tuition plus stipends for dissertation support, travel, and conference expenses ($2.5M grant funding 4 scholars at each university)
eligibility: Doctoral students in special education at the University of Maryland or Vanderbilt University pursuing leadership roles in higher education, school districts, or research organizations
notes: Includes DC-area internships (UMD-based students), joint summer intensives, and monthly cross-campus virtual seminars.
location: University of Maryland and Vanderbilt University

organization: National Center for Leadership in Intensive Intervention (Vanderbilt, UConn, UIC, U Minnesota, UT Austin, U Georgia, Michigan State) — OSEP-funded
name: NCLII-2 Doctoral Scholars Program
opens: Varies by partner institution's doctoral admissions cycle
deadline: Not specified; contact nclii@vanderbilt.edu or partner institution
amount: Tuition, stipend, and research funding ($6.4M, 5-year grant funding 28 doctoral scholars across the consortium)
eligibility: Doctoral students in special education at one of the seven consortium universities focused on intensive-intervention research for students with disabilities
notes: Scholars owe 2 years of field service per year of academic funding received.

name: Project PASS-IT
amount: 15 credits of tuition and fees covered annually, plus a stipend for books and supplies ($1.2M grant supporting 36 scholars over 5 years)
eligibility: Students enrolled in master's-level special education or doctoral-level school psychology programs at Minnesota State University, Mankato
notes: Interdisciplinary training pairing future special education teachers with school psychologists to serve students with high-intensity needs.

organization: Merrimack College, School of Education and Social Policy
name: K-12 Teacher Education Fellowship
deadline: Rolling, first-come-first-served (2026 placements run August 2026 through June 2027/2028)
eligibility: Admitted students in Merrimack's M.Ed. in Teacher Education (Elementary, Moderate Disabilities, ESL, or Middle/High School concentrations) who complete a year-long PreK-12 clinical residency at a partner Massachusetts school
notes: Fellowship placement is not guaranteed upon program admission; requires reliable transportation to the residency site and attendance at on-campus evening coursework.

name: Urban Education Fellowship
opens: Tied to MAT/UEP graduate application cycle
deadline: Matches the MAT/UEP program's graduate application deadline
amount: Free tuition via a loan-forgiveness structure, for up to 10 admitted students per year
eligibility: Admitted domestic students (F-1 visa holders ineligible) in Brown's Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) or Urban Education Policy (UEP) master's program, who commit to 3 years of service in Rhode Island urban schools (MAT) or public-sector/nonprofit education organizations (UEP)
notes: Structured as annual federal loan deferment and eventual cancellation rather than a direct cash award; apply via the program's Financial Information application section.
duration: 1-year master's degree, plus a 3-year post-graduation service commitment

organization: Yale University, Office of New Haven Affairs (with Southern Connecticut State University)
name: Yale Teaching Fellowship Program
amount: Full tuition plus a $47,380 living stipend in year one (Teacher Pipeline Track)
eligibility: College graduates and New Haven Public Schools paraprofessionals/student-facing staff (Teacher Pipeline Track), or certified teachers (Current Teachers Track); requires a 3-year post-graduation teaching commitment in New Haven Public Schools
notes: Degree conferred through Southern Connecticut State University; includes ongoing mentorship during the service commitment.
duration: 2 years (MAT, Teacher Pipeline Track) or 4 semesters (M.S., Current Teachers Track)

organization: The Hotchkiss School, in partnership with the Klingenstein Center, Teachers College, Columbia University
name: Walter J. Crain Fellowship
amount: Full sponsorship of tuition, books, fees, and housing for the MA in Private School Leadership at Teachers College
eligibility: Educators with 5+ years of professional experience in a school or higher-education setting who aspire to independent-school leadership and demonstrate strong cultural competency and commitment to working with BIPOC students; combines a teaching role at Hotchkiss with earning a master's degree
flags: Job-embedded fellowship; 5-year prior-experience requirement
notes: Structured as a paid faculty appointment at Hotchkiss plus a fully funded graduate degree rather than a stipend-only fellowship. Included under the pathway-to-graduate-study rule since it explicitly funds a master's degree, but the 5-year-experience bar and embedded job make it closer to mid-career than most entries on this list.
duration: 3-4 year Hotchkiss appointment, funding one year of graduate study within it
location: Lakeville, Connecticut (Hotchkiss); degree from Teachers College, Columbia University

organization: University of Colorado Boulder, School of Education
name: Miramontes-Baca Doctoral Scholars Program
opens: Tied to PhD in Education admissions cycle
deadline: Check CU Boulder School of Education PhD admissions deadline
amount: 5 years of full funding for doctoral study (tuition plus stipend), including one dedicated dissertation-writing year
eligibility: Admitted PhD in Education students with research interests in educational equity and cultural diversity; students from underrepresented groups and first-generation college graduates are encouraged to apply
notes: Named for professors Ofelia Miramontes and Leonard Baca, both known for research on educational equity; scholars join a dedicated cohort community.

name: Tuition-Free Fellowship, M.Ed. in Teaching Special Education
deadline: Not specified; apply as early as possible given limited slots
amount: 100% of graduate tuition covered by the partner school district; graduation and technology fees, books, and health insurance remain the student's responsibility
eligibility: Admitted students in Regis College's M.Ed. in Teaching Special Education who complete a year-long PK-12 residency at a partner Massachusetts school district
notes: Small ancillary fees (graduation, technology) apply on top of the tuition waiver.
duration: 1 year (summer coursework start, fall residency, spring graduation)
location: Weston, Massachusetts, with district residency placements

organization: American Association of Hispanics in Higher Education (AAHHE)
name: Graduate Student Fellows Program (GSFP)
opens: Cycle currently open for the 2027 cohort; check site for exact dates
deadline: Varies by year; check aahhe.org for the current GSFP deadline
amount: No direct cash stipend confirmed; provides mentoring, dissertation/research feedback, job-search preparation, and conference/travel networking support (verify current-year specifics with AAHHE)
eligibility: Current doctoral students in any discipline preparing for careers in academia or postsecondary administration/policy; open to all applicants regardless of race or ethnicity per AAHHE policy, though the program centers support for Hispanic/Latino/Latinx doctoral scholars
flags: Cross-disciplinary eligibility; verify whether a cash stipend is included in the current cycle
notes: Not limited to education PhDs by discipline, but explicitly supports doctoral students pursuing higher-education administration and policy careers, which overlaps closely with the ed-leadership pipeline.
duration: Roughly 1 year of active mentoring, tied to the annual AAHHE conference cycle

organization: Translational Data Analytics Institute (TDAI), The Ohio State University
name: Translational Data Analytics Institute AI and Data Science Graduate Fellows Program (TDAI)
deadline: ~July 1 annually (2026 cycle closed; next cycle expected June–July 2027)
amount: TDAI covers 50% of salary/benefits/tuition/fees (exact $ varies by home department) plus up to $1,000/yr for conference travel
eligibility: Ohio State PhD candidates (dissertation-stage doctoral students who have passed their candidacy exam) from ANY discipline whose research involves AI or data science; requires a TDAI-member faculty advisor.
notes: Two-year interdisciplinary fellowship beginning Fall 2026. Verified via official TDAI page. Deadline already passed for this year's cycle but program runs annually.

organization: Hawai'i Data Science Institute (HIDSI), University of Hawai'i
name: AI @ HIDSI Fellows Program
deadline: Rolling / Not specified (Fall 2026–Spring 2027 cohort currently recruiting)
amount: Research support and mentorship (no direct stipend figure published); NSF-funded initiative
eligibility: Graduate students CURRENTLY ENROLLED at the University of Hawai'i in a Master's or PhD program, in good academic standing, with a current research mentor.
notes: NSF-funded cyberinfrastructure-skills initiative; 44 participants since 2018. Apply via Google form linked on the page.

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
deadline: ~November 16 annually (2026 cycle closed; check site for next call)
amount: Up to $40,000/year living stipend for exceptional candidates, plus conference and compute budgets
eligibility: BOTH current PhD students AND prospective PhD applicants (about to enroll) worldwide, working on cooperative AI (multi-agent systems, game theory, mechanism design applied to AI).
notes: Lightweight application process; up to 3 years of funding contingent on continued cooperative-AI research.

name: RBC Borealis Graduate Fellowship
deadline: ~January 25 annually (2025–26 cycle closed; next cycle expected ~Nov 2026–Jan 2027)
eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or international students pursuing a graduate degree (Master's or PhD) in machine learning or AI at a Canadian university.
notes: Also includes opportunity to co-publish with an RBC Borealis researcher. Formerly branded 'Borealis AI.'

name: Turing PhD Enrichment Scheme
deadline: ~March annually (2025–26 call closed; next call expected ~early 2027)
amount: Funded placement — stipend/travel and professional-development funding per Turing terms (exact figure set per call)
eligibility: Full-time PhD students at Turing university-network institutions in the UK working in data science or AI-relevant research areas.
notes: 9-month, in-person placement embedded in a Turing research team (Health, Environment, Defence & National Security, or Fundamental Data Science/AI research).

name: Snap Research Fellowship
deadline: Not specified — annual cycle, check page for current call
eligibility: PhD or Master's students currently enrolled at any accredited university worldwide doing research in computer science areas relevant to Snap (AR, ML, computer vision, NLP, etc.).
notes: Info page URL retains a '2022' slug but is the live, canonical description of the ongoing program; confirm current-year call before applying.

name: Adobe India AI Research Fellowship
amount: ₹12,00,000 (~US$14,000) stipend, paid upfront, plus free Adobe software access for one year
eligibility: Full-time PhD candidates enrolled at recognized universities IN INDIA with at least 12 months remaining before completing their degree, researching AI (computer vision, NLP, human-centered design, etc.).
notes: International (India-based) fellowship — a good example of a non-US technical AI fellowship.

organization: Lucy Family Institute for Data & Society, University of Notre Dame
name: Lucy Graduate Scholars Program
deadline: ~late March annually (2026–28 cohort call closed; next call TBA on site)
eligibility: Full-time enrolled Notre Dame graduate students from ANY department doing interdisciplinary data-science-related research; preference given to students starting their 2nd or 3rd year.
notes: Scholars serve as research-community leaders/ambassadors for the Institute in addition to receiving funding.

name: Ken Kennedy Institute Computational Science & Engineering Graduate Recruiting Fellowship
deadline: Not specified — departments nominate candidates; contact kenkennedy@rice.edu for current-cycle dates
amount: $15,000 total stipend enhancement, paid monthly over 4 years (~$3,750/year)
eligibility: Incoming/prospective PhD applicants to Rice University science & engineering departments researching AI, high-performance computing, or computational science & engineering; each department may nominate up to 3 candidates.
notes: Prospective/incoming-graduate-student fellowship — a pathway-style recruiting award, awarded via department nomination rather than direct student application.

organization: American Epilepsy Society (jointly with Epilepsy Foundation)
name: AES/Epilepsy Foundation Predoctoral Research Fellowship
deadline: Historically mid-January (verify current cycle at aesnet.org)
amount: Up to $30,000 (stipend + annual-meeting travel) for one year
other_benefits: One-year AES membership included.
eligibility: Full-time PhD students pursuing dissertation research with an epilepsy-relevant theme, under a mentor with epilepsy research expertise, at a US institution.
flags: None identified.
notes: Smaller disease-focused society fellowship, distinct from the big NIH/NSF programs already indexed.

organization: UCSF Larry L. Hillblom Center for the Biology of Aging / Bakar Aging Research Institute (BARI)
name: Hillblom Center / BARI Graduate Student Fellowship
amount: Stipend supplement amount not publicly listed — verify current figure with BARI/Hillblom Center
other_benefits: Access to weekly Biology of Aging journal club and annual 'Molecules to Medicine' symposium.
eligibility: UCSF graduate students entering their 3rd year or beyond (including international students) whose faculty mentor is a BARI member; research focused on the biology of aging.
flags: University-restricted (UCSF graduate students only).
notes: University-hosted, regional (single-campus) fellowship for aging biology, not a national program.

name: National Ataxia Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship (NAF)
deadline: Not specified — applications via proposalCENTRAL, check ataxia.org for current cycle
other_benefits: Open to basic, translational, and clinical ataxia research of any type.
eligibility: Currently enrolled PhD (or PharmD/PsyD/ScD) students, including MD/PhD or other combined professional/research doctoral students, who have completed qualifying exams and are pursuing ataxia-relevant research.
flags: None identified.
notes: Small rare-disease foundation fellowship, unlikely to be already indexed.

organization: Alpha Omega Alpha (AΩA) Honor Medical Society
name: Carolyn L. Kuckein Student Research Fellowship
deadline: January 19 (annual; verify current-year date on alphaomegaalpha.org)
amount: $7,000 total ($3,000 on award, $3,000 on final report) plus up to $1,000 conference travel
other_benefits: Travel reimbursement to present research at a national meeting.
eligibility: First- or second-year medical (professional-degree) students at schools with active AΩA chapters; students on a research year off or PhD students are not eligible for this particular award.
flags: Nominated one-per-chapter; excludes PhD/MD-PhD students taking a dedicated research year, but included per audience rule as a professional-degree (MD) student program.
notes: Honor-society fellowship for early-stage medical students, not a household-name biomedical program.
location: United States medical schools with AΩA chapters

name: Hematology Inclusion Pathway (HIP) Graduate Student Award (formerly Minority Hematology Graduate Award)
deadline: Not specified — check hematology.org for current cycle
other_benefits: Complimentary ASH membership through graduate school; travel to ASH Annual Meeting; mentoring/reception events.
eligibility: First-, second-, or third-year graduate (PhD) students in the US, Canada, or Mexico from communities underrepresented in hematology, pursuing an academic hematology career.
flags: Identity-specific (underrepresented groups in hematology).
notes: Discipline-society, identity-specific program; part of a longitudinal 13-year ASH pathway most people only know at later career stages.

name: Sarnoff Fellowship Program
deadline: Not specified — check sarnofffoundation.org for current cycle (historically January)
amount: Full-year stipend plus research/travel support (exact figure not published in available sources — verify on site)
other_benefits: Personalized mentorship from leading cardiovascular scientists.
eligibility: Second- or third-year students at accredited US medical schools (MD only — MD/PhD students are not eligible) taking a year to conduct cardiovascular research.
flags: Excludes MD/PhD students; open only to MD-track (professional-degree) students, which satisfies the audience rule.
notes: Well-regarded within cardiology circles but not a mainstream, broadly-indexed name.

name: KidneyCure Pre-Doctoral Fellowship Award Program
deadline: Cycle recently closed — check kidneycure.org for next application window (historically fall)
other_benefits: Sponsor/mentor must demonstrate sufficient funding for the mentee's full fellowship period.
eligibility: Current PhD students in an accredited doctoral program who have passed qualifying exams (if applicable), do not yet hold an MD/PhD/DO/equivalent terminal degree, committing ≥75% time to kidney-relevant dissertation research.
flags: Application currently closed — confirm reopening date.
notes: Discipline-society (nephrology) fellowship housed under ASN's KidneyCure initiative, not broadly indexed.
location: Not restricted to US per search, verify residency requirements on site

name: Porter Physiology Development Fellowship
deadline: Historically mid-January (verify current cycle at physiology.org)
other_benefits: Professional development programming, networking, and travel awards to the APS Summit.
eligibility: Full-time PhD/DSc students in the physiological sciences at US institutions, from underrepresented racial/ethnic groups (per NIH diversity criteria), who are US citizens/permanent residents.
flags: Identity/diversity-specific eligibility.
notes: Long-running (APS) diversity fellowship in physiology that's easy to overlook next to bigger NIH diversity programs.
duration: 1 year, renewable for a 2nd year based on progress

name: Jack and Fay Netchin Medical Student Summer Fellowship
deadline: LOI ~December, full application ~March (verify current cycle at abta.org)
other_benefits: Mentored placement with an experienced brain tumor researcher.
eligibility: Medical (MD/DO, professional-degree) students spending a summer conducting brain tumor research with a scientist mentor.
flags: Small award; summer-only.
notes: ABTA is best known for its postdoctoral fellowships; this medical-student summer award is much less visible.

name: Neuroscience Scholars Program (NSP)
deadline: Not specified — check sfn.org for current annual cycle
amount: Non-stipend fellowship: mentoring, professional development, and travel awards (up to 15 Fellows/year); funded via a $1.35M NINDS grant
other_benefits: Live events/webinars, online diversity affinity group, career-advancement mentoring; won the 2018 Presidential Award for Excellence in Science Mentoring.
eligibility: Graduate students (or postdoctoral fellows) enrolled in a degree-granting program in neuroscience or related biomedical/behavioral/clinical/social sciences, from groups underrepresented in these fields (Black/African American, Hispanic/Latino, American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, or individuals with disabilities).
flags: Open to postdocs as well as grad students — qualifies per audience rule since grad students are eligible.
notes: Mentoring/career-development fellowship rather than direct research funding, so it can be missed by indexes focused only on stipend awards.

name: St. Baldrick's Summer Fellowship Award
deadline: Not specified — apply via ProposalCentral, check stbaldricks.org for current cycle
other_benefits: Mentor serves as PI; positions students within active childhood cancer research programs.
eligibility: Undergraduate, graduate, or medical school students working in a pediatric oncology research setting for a summer under a faculty mentor.
flags: Application submitted by mentor as PI, with student as fellow.
notes: St. Baldrick's is known for its head-shaving fundraising brand, so its research fellowships are often overlooked relative to NCI/ASCO-type programs.
location: US and Canadian pediatric oncology research sites

name: Equal Justice America Summer Fellowship
amount: Up to $5,000 (max $15,000 total with other funding)
other_benefits: Grant can be combined with other funding sources up to $15,000 total
eligibility: Current law students (any year) at a qualifying U.S. law school who secure a full-time (35 hrs/wk), minimum 8-week unpaid/underpaid summer placement at a civil legal services organization (not public defender or government offices).
flags: No fee confirmed
notes: National program funding law students nationwide who arrange their own civil legal aid summer placement; no application fee.

organization: NYU School of Law, Center on Civil Justice
name: Access to Justice Summer Fellowship
other_benefits: Symposium presentation, published research
eligibility: Rising 2L and 3L students at NYU School of Law (2-3 positions).
flags: NYU students only
notes: Fellows research and write a policy paper on a state-court access-to-justice issue and present at an end-of-summer symposium.

organization: Temple University Beasley School of Law
name: Rubin-Presser Social Justice Fellows Program
amount: Scholarship funding plus up to $5,250 summer work-study match and $1,000 public-interest internship stipend annually
other_benefits: Mentoring, leadership development
eligibility: Incoming (admitted) JD students at Temple Law, day or evening division, committed to public interest law.
flags: Temple Law incoming students only
notes: Selective program for incoming students demonstrating public-interest commitment and leadership.

name: Legal Fellowship Sponsorship Program
amount: Salary guaranteed at no less than $76,100/year (ACLU supplements external fellowship stipend)
other_benefits: Health insurance, 5 weeks vacation, 401(k) match
eligibility: Rising 3L law students, judicial clerks, or recent law-school graduates who will obtain a JD and Florida Bar admission by fellowship start; ACLU-FL sponsors the applicant for external funding (e.g., Skadden, Equal Justice Works).
flags: Requires external fellowship funding award
notes: Applicant develops a project proposal with ACLU-FL and applies with their sponsorship to national fellowship funders; fellowship begins Fall 2027.

organization: University of Texas School of Law, William Wayne Justice Center for Public Interest Law
name: Environmental Justice Fellowship
eligibility: Current UT Law 3L students or UT Law alumni completing a judicial clerkship immediately after graduation; must secure a 501(c)(3) host organization.
flags: UT Law affiliation required
notes: Two-year postgraduate fellowship; priority to Texas-based environmental justice work with groups like Earthjustice, Sierra Club, Save Our Springs Alliance.

organization: California Lawyers Association, Environmental Law Section
name: Environmental Law Diversity & Inclusion Fellowship
other_benefits: Mentorship, free conference registration (Yosemite Environmental Law Conference)
eligibility: Current law students (priority to 1Ls/2Ls; 3Ls not sitting for the Bar that summer may apply) who become CLA Environmental Law Section members (free student membership available).
notes: Funds an 8-10 week summer internship at a California government agency or public-interest org in environmental, energy, land use, or natural resources law.

name: Catalyst Public Interest Fellowship Program
deadline: Rolling annual (recent cycles closed mid-April/mid-May; check tnybf.org for current dates)
eligibility: First-year (1L) law students at New York law schools taking otherwise-unpaid public interest summer internships.
flags: NY law students only
notes: 10-year-running program ($4M+ distributed) placing ~60 fellows/year across 30+ NY public interest organizations (legal services, DA's offices, government agencies).

name: University of Connecticut Humanities Institute Dissertation Fellowship (UCHI)
opens: Applications open via Interfolio in fall (~November)
amount: Full academic-year assistantship stipend plus research/travel/photocopying funds
other_benefits: Health benefits, office space, research/travel funds
eligibility: Current UConn PhD candidates in humanities disciplines who have completed qualifying exams, prospectus, and sufficient research to finish the dissertation during the fellowship year; may not be scheduled to defend in the fall semester
flags: UConn PhD students only
notes: Up to 4 dissertation scholars/year, including the named Draper and Richard Brown Dissertation Fellowships. Fellows are in continuous residence, attend weekly colloquia, and give a public lecture. Apply via Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/175403

organization: Rutgers University, Center for Cultural Analysis (CCA)
name: Rutgers University, Center for Cultural Analysis Graduate Fellowship (CCA)
opens: Varies by cycle; calls typically issued in winter for the following academic year
deadline: Not posted for next cycle at time of research — contact admin@cca.rutgers.edu to confirm current deadline
amount: $25,000 stipend plus tuition remission (up to 3 credits/semester) and health benefits (2017-18 figures; confirm current amount)
other_benefits: Office space, participation in interdisciplinary seminar
eligibility: Current Rutgers PhD students in dissertation stage with 5 or fewer years of Rutgers funding (waiver possible for 6+ years if seminar theme fits dissertation)
flags: Rutgers students only; confirm current-cycle deadline directly with CCA
notes: Roughly 5 graduate fellowships/year tied to an annual interdisciplinary seminar theme; year-long dissertation residency

organization: University of Michigan, LSA Institute for the Humanities
name: Institute for the Humanities Graduate Student Fellowship
amount: Not specified on public page (standard 10-month fellowship stipend)
other_benefits: Office space, seminar participation
eligibility: University of Michigan graduate students who have attained (or will attain) PhD candidacy by the fellowship start; not open to current/former Rackham Predoctoral Fellows
flags: University of Michigan students only
notes: 10-month residential fellowship (Sept 2–June 30) with weekly interdisciplinary fellows seminar; requires dissertation description, personal statement, and writing sample

organization: Northwestern University, Alice Kaplan Institute for the Humanities
name: Franke Graduate Fellowship
deadline: Not specified on public page — see Institute's Graduate Application Instructions page for current-cycle date
amount: Two quarters of full tuition, a monthly stipend, and $2,000 in research funds
other_benefits: Dissertation working groups, Future Directions Forum participation
eligibility: Northwestern doctoral students in their 4th, 5th, or 6th year pursuing independent humanities research in Weinberg or Bienen programs
flags: Northwestern students only
notes: Fellows join weekly lunch seminars and dissertation working groups, and teach a self-designed course in spring quarter; funding can be 'banked' from an earlier year for later use

organization: Cornell University, Society for the Humanities
name: Mellon Graduate Fellowship
amount: $35,661 stipend plus College of Arts & Sciences tuition waiver and health insurance
other_benefits: Tuition waiver, health insurance
eligibility: Cornell graduate students in humanities departments/programs in the College of Arts & Sciences who have completed the A exam and all degree requirements except the dissertation; typically 4th-6th year students
flags: Cornell students only
notes: Two positions/year; residential at the A.D. White House; weekly Fellows Seminar workshopping projects around an annual focal theme

organization: University of Pennsylvania, Wolf Humanities Center
name: Penn Doctoral Research Fellowship
other_benefits: Seminar and symposium participation
eligibility: Penn dissertation-level (ABD) graduate students in the humanities with an approved prospectus; research must relate to the Center's annual theme (2026-27: 'Practice')
flags: Penn students only
notes: Fellows attend the weekly Mellon Research Seminar, present their own work, respond to a colleague's paper, and help plan a one-day symposium. Apply via Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/168941

name: Evan Frankel Fellowship for PhD Students in the Humanities
deadline: Late November (annual; exact date announced each cycle)
amount: Graduate School-recommended 9-month Arts & Sciences stipend plus tuition, mandatory fees, and (for those enrolling in Duke's plan) health insurance
other_benefits: Health insurance premium coverage
eligibility: Duke PhD students in a Humanities program, in good standing, who have completed preliminary exams and expect their final doctoral year during the fellowship term; departments may nominate up to two students
flags: Duke students only; requires departmental nomination
notes: Two fellowships awarded annually for advanced students in the write-up stage; requires departmental nomination plus DGS and advisor letters

organization: University of Washington, Simpson Center for the Humanities
name: Society of Scholars Graduate Fellowship
amount: Academic-year track: two quarters of support incl. benefits, tuition waiver, and $1,500 research budget; Summer track: $10,000 (no benefits/tuition)
other_benefits: Tuition waiver (academic-year track), research budget
eligibility: UW doctoral students who have advanced to candidacy by the submission deadline and will receive no other funding during the award term
flags: UW students only
notes: Single application pool considered for both the academic-year cohort and a newly created summer dissertation-fellowship cohort; in-person biweekly (academic year) or weekly (summer) meetings required
duration: Two quarters (academic year) or one summer

organization: Emory University, Fox Center for Humanistic Inquiry
name: Dissertation Completion Fellowship
deadline: Early December (annual; 2026-27 cohort selection closed — next cycle opens ~Sept 2026)
amount: 9-month stipend plus full health-insurance subsidy and $1,500 research/conference stipend
other_benefits: Dedicated workspace, weekly Fellows' Seminar
eligibility: Advanced Emory College/Laney Graduate School PhD candidates whose dissertation can be completed and approved within the fellowship year
flags: Emory/Laney students only
notes: Up to 3 fellowships/year tied to an annual theme (2026-27: 'Habitat'); dedicated Fox Center workspace and mandatory weekly Fellows' Seminar; outside teaching/work prohibited

organization: Johns Hopkins University, Alexander Grass Humanities Institute (AGHI)
name: Johns Hopkins University, Alexander Grass Humanities Institute Graduate Research Fellowship (AGHI)
amount: Full KSAS stipend plus tuition costs equal to 20% of resident-student tuition, for one semester
other_benefits: AGHI workspace access
eligibility: JHU PhD students in one of 13 KSAS humanities departments/programs, typically in their 4th-6th year, in the final stages of the dissertation with high likelihood of completing within the fellowship year
flags: JHU students only; institute's own site blocked automated fetch, but program is corroborated by multiple independent sources
notes: Fellowship replaces the semester's teaching requirement; fellows meet biweekly with a faculty mentor to workshop the dissertation. Apply via Interfolio: http://apply.interfolio.com/160475

organization: Brown University, Cogut Institute for the Humanities
name: Cogut Institute Graduate Fellowship
amount: Teaching relief plus office space and up to $1,000 in travel/research funds
other_benefits: Office space at the Institute
eligibility: Brown doctoral students in the 3rd, 4th, or 5th year of a humanities or humanistic-social-science program, applying to hold the fellowship the following year; must have advanced to candidacy by the fellowship start
flags: Brown students only
notes: Year-long weekly research seminar; application requires a dissertation abstract, progress statement, writing sample, two letters, and a DGS letter of good standing

organization: Vanderbilt University, Robert Penn Warren Center for the Humanities
name: Graduate Theme Fellowship
deadline: Not specified on public page — contact the Center for the current cycle's deadline
amount: $2,000 stipend, paid in two installments (fall and spring)
other_benefits: Cohort community, public presentation opportunity
eligibility: Vanderbilt graduate students from any school with a well-defined humanities or humanistic-social-science project who have completed at least one year of their program
flags: Vanderbilt students only; deadline not published — contact matthew.dicintio@vanderbilt.edu
notes: Small cohort explores the Center's annual theme through biweekly meetings; culminates in a research project, creative work, or public-engagement project with a final presentation. Residential/in-person participation required

organization: Washington University in St. Louis, Center for the Humanities
name: Graduate Student Fellowship
other_benefits: Workspace at the Center, interdisciplinary community
eligibility: WashU graduate students in good standing in a humanities department who are in the dissertation-writing stage and not holding a concurrent teaching or research assistantship
flags: WashU students only
notes: Fall and spring cohorts each year; requires a DGS approval letter confirming no concurrent mentored teaching/research and an 800-word dissertation narrative

organization: University of Kansas, Hall Center for the Humanities
name: Richard and Jeannette Sias Graduate Fellowship in the Humanities
amount: $9,000 stipend plus up to $500 expense reimbursement, one credit hour of tuition, and a health-insurance subsidy
other_benefits: Office space at the Hall Center
eligibility: KU doctoral students in humanities-oriented research who have an approved dissertation proposal/prospectus and hold no other paid position during the fellowship semester
flags: KU students only
notes: Two fellowships/year, one semester each (Fall 2026 or Spring 2027); application submitted via the Hall Center Competitions Portal

organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Humanities Research Institute (HRI)
name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Humanities Research Institute Campus Graduate Fellowship (HRI)
amount: $25,000 stipend plus tuition and partial fee waiver
other_benefits: Seminar participation
eligibility: Current UIUC Urbana PhD students (ABD, prelims complete) or 2nd-year MFA students in good standing who have not previously held this fellowship
flags: UIUC Urbana students only
notes: Tied to an annual theme (2026-27: 'Sovereignties'); fellows must reside within 20 miles of campus and attend a biweekly Fellows Seminar in person

name: Graduate Student Summer Research Fellowship
deadline: March 1 (annual; most recently confirmed for March 1, 2024 cycle — verify current-year date on site)
amount: $10,000 (plus specialized East Asian Studies and Health Humanities & Ethics tracks at $10,000 each)
other_benefits: Participation in Humanities Center intellectual community
eligibility: Pitt PhD students admitted to candidacy (ABD, post-prospectus review) in a humanities or humanities-adjacent doctoral program, resident in Pittsburgh during the fellowship year
flags: Pitt students only; confirm current-year deadline on site
notes: Tied to an annual theme (e.g., 'Method?'); supports drafting dissertation chapters over the summer, shared with the Center's community during the following academic year

organization: University of Notre Dame, Nanovic Institute for European Studies
name: Nanovic Institute Graduate Fellowship
amount: Not specified on public page; related named Nanovic dissertation funds (Annese/Tobin) have historically awarded up to $25,000
other_benefits: Not specified
eligibility: Notre Dame graduate students from any field (e.g., Medieval Institute, political science, peace studies) whose dissertation research engages Europe or European ideas
flags: Notre Dame students only; program availability and exact terms vary by year — verify before applying
notes: Up to 10 fellows/year; priority given to projects aligned with Institute research priorities. Availability has varied year to year (the Institute was unable to offer a dissertation fellowship in 2024-25) — confirm current-cycle offering with Roy Kimmey (rkimmey@nd.edu) before applying
duration: Varies by cycle (historically up to a full academic year)

organization: University of Oregon, Oregon Humanities Center
name: Dissertation Fellowship
amount: One-term GE3 (.49 FTE) research-appointment salary, tuition waiver (up to 16 credits), fee subsidy (all but $61), and health insurance (95% university-covered)
other_benefits: Optional office space at OHC
eligibility: University of Oregon doctoral students advanced to candidacy (ABD) conducting research for/writing an approved dissertation in a humanities-related field, in any department
flags: University of Oregon students only
notes: Must expect to defend within one year of the fellowship term and may not teach during the term; requires a Work-in-Progress talk and a brief post-fellowship report

name: American Folklore Society Graduate Fieldwork Grant (AFS)
other_benefits: None specified beyond the award
eligibility: Full-time graduate students (PhD students in folklore or related fields, or terminal MA students committed to continuing to a doctorate) in good standing, with at least one AFS-active folklorist on their committee. No citizenship restriction.
flags: Requires AFS membership.
notes: Supports dissertation/thesis fieldwork projects grounded in long-term ethnographic engagement; one award per student lifetime.

name: John Hope Franklin Dissertation Fellowship
other_benefits: Access to APS Library & Museum collections
eligibility: Doctoral students admitted to candidacy at an American university (or exceptional American doctoral students abroad) who have completed all coursework and are ready to devote 12 full-time months to dissertation research/writing.
flags: No membership fee required to apply.
notes: Named for historian John Hope Franklin; fellow expected to spend significant time in residence at the APS Library.

name: Friends of the APS Predoctoral Fellowship
amount: $25,000 stipend plus $5,000 travel/research fund (9-month residential fellowship)
other_benefits: Access to APS collections and scholarly community
eligibility: Advanced PhD candidates (any field) working toward dissertation completion whose research requires APS Library & Museum collections.
flags: No application fee.
notes: Open to US citizens and foreign nationals, though no visa sponsorship is provided.

name: John C. Slater Predoctoral Fellowship in the History of Science, Technology, and Medicine
other_benefits: Access to APS collections
eligibility: Advanced PhD candidates working toward dissertation completion on topics in the history of science, technology, or medicine.
flags: No application fee.
notes: Fellow expected to be in residence at the APS Library & Museum in Philadelphia.

name: 21st Century Fellowship
deadline: Annual, ~April 1 (verify on site; has varied by year)
other_benefits: None specified beyond award
eligibility: PhD candidates in ethnomusicology who will hold ABD (all-but-dissertation) status by August 1 of the application year, committing to at least 6 months of dissertation fieldwork (onsite or virtual).
flags: Requires current SEM membership.
notes: Supports dissertation fieldwork research; recipients often present at the SEM Annual Meeting.

name: Howard Mayer Brown Fellowship
deadline: Annual, ~early February (same cycle as AMS 50 Fellowship)
other_benefits: None specified
eligibility: Graduate students who have completed at least one year of full-time graduate work, intend to pursue a musicology PhD, and are in good standing at a US or Canadian university.
flags: Restricted to members of historically underrepresented groups in musicology (e.g., tribal community members, HBCU graduates).
notes: Established to increase presence of scholars from historically underrepresented groups in musicology.

name: Summer Economics Fellows Program
amount: Stipend varies by sponsoring institution (contact program for current figures)
other_benefits: Mentorship and institutional research access
eligibility: Open to senior graduate students in economics (as well as postdoctoral scholars and junior faculty); graduate applicants must have a faculty recommender.
flags: Open to grad students and non-students alike; no fee to apply.
notes: Places fellows at sponsoring research institutions for a summer research placement; designed to increase participation of women and underrepresented minorities in economics.

name: Allan R. Millett Dissertation Research Fellowship
other_benefits: None specified
eligibility: Full-time graduate students in an accredited doctoral program conducting dissertation research in any field of military history.
flags: Requires Society for Military History membership.
notes: Requires a 3-page proposal, CV, and letter of support.

name: Schallek Fellowship
other_benefits: None specified beyond stipend
eligibility: Graduate students (PhD candidates) at any stage of dissertation research/writing whose work focuses on the late medieval period in England/British Isles or British Continental connections.
flags: Requires Medieval Academy of America membership; topical/geographic scope restriction (late medieval Britain).
notes: One of the largest dissertation fellowships offered by a discipline society for medieval studies; funding begins the following September.

name: Dissertation Research Grants (Paul Vouras Fund and others)
other_benefits: None specified
eligibility: PhD candidates in geography (any specialty) who have completed all doctoral requirements except the dissertation by the semester following the award.
flags: Requires 1 year of AAG membership prior to application; Vouras Fund gives preference to minority applicants.
notes: Paul Vouras Fund gives preference to minority student applicants; Otis Paul Starkey Fund supports US/territorial regional studies.

organization: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Foundation Graduate Awards (AIAA)
deadline: Annual, January 31 (online application); Feb 14 for recommendation letters
amount: $5,000–$10,000 (varies by named award, including Orville and Wilbur Wright Graduate Award)
other_benefits: Opportunity to present research at an AIAA conference
eligibility: Graduate students conducting research in air and space sciences, minimum 3.3 GPA, at least one term of full-time graduate work completed with an approved research topic.
flags: Requires current AIAA Student membership.
notes: Wright Graduate Award allows enrollment at any accredited university worldwide; other awards limited to US/territories.

name: Paul Oskar Kristeller Fellowship
other_benefits: None specified
eligibility: RSA members at all career stages, including graduate students and PhD candidates researching the Renaissance period (1300-1700), for non-Art History topics.
flags: Requires 12 months of prior RSA membership.
notes: Funds may cover research travel, archive access fees, digital images/permissions, and other project costs.

organization: United Nations University International Institute for Global Health (UNU-IIGH)
name: Global Health PhD Fellowship Programme
deadline: Check current cycle on site (opens/closes annually)
amount: USD $1,000/month subsistence allowance; travel grant possible for LMIC candidates
other_benefits: Direct UN policy engagement, applied research training
eligibility: Currently enrolled PhD candidates in global health, public health, health policy, or related field who have completed doctoral fieldwork
notes: 6-12 month placement in Kuala Lumpur working directly with UN global health policy processes.

name: Health Justice Fellowship
opens: Annually in July (subscribe to newsletter for exact date)
other_benefits: Cohort-based mentorship and leadership training
eligibility: Currently enrolled students in good standing at U.S. medical, dental, nursing, physician associate, or public health schools
notes: 9-month virtual program for trainees committed to advancing health justice within health professions education.

organization: Samuel DuBois Cook Center on Social Equity, Duke University
name: Graduate Summer Research Fellowship (Health Equity pillar)
other_benefits: Faculty mentorship, research network
eligibility: Current Duke University PhD students in good standing, enrolled for the following fall semester
flags: Duke-affiliated students only
notes: Fellows connect to one of the Cook Center's research pillars, including Health Equity, plus data science/methods themes.

organization: NC State University Global One Health Academy
name: Global One Health Fellows
opens: Called for annually (2026-27 cohort call issued Nov 2025)
amount: $34,000 stipend, plus tuition and insurance coverage (1 year)
other_benefits: Interdisciplinary mentorship, professional development, networking
eligibility: Current or incoming PhD students at NC State (early-career PhD students preferred; later-career PhD students eligible with 1+ year remaining)
flags: NC State PhD students/admits only
notes: Interdisciplinary training spanning human, animal, plant, and environmental health (One Health framework).

organization: Morris K. Udall and Stewart L. Udall Foundation
name: Native American Graduate Fellowship (health care track)
amount: Up to $25,000 (up to 3 awards anticipated in 2026)
other_benefits: Leadership network, alumni community
eligibility: Native American/Alaska Native graduate students currently pursuing advanced degrees in health-related fields (health administration, health education, public health, policy, research, etc.)
flags: Native American/Alaska Native applicants only
notes: Federally chartered foundation fellowship supporting future Native health-care leaders.

organization: University at Albany, SUNY (Center for the Elimination of Minority Health Disparities)
name: Presidential Doctoral Fellowship for Research Training in Health Disparities
deadline: February 1 annually (essay due for the cohort starting that year)
amount: Full tuition & mandatory fees (4 years) + $18,000 compensation + personal computer + travel support
other_benefits: Professional association membership, transdisciplinary training
eligibility: Applicants admitted to a UAlbany doctoral program interested in health disparities research (open to all applicants, not limited by background)
notes: Funded via a $10M NIMHD endowment grant (2016); includes professional association memberships.

organization: University of Michigan Institute for Healthcare Policy & Innovation (IHPI)
name: HSR Student Fellowship & Internship Program
other_benefits: Faculty mentorship, HSR training
eligibility: Currently enrolled UM doctoral, medical, or pharmacy students (Fellowship track); incoming UM graduate/doctoral students starting fall 2026 also eligible
flags: University of Michigan students/incoming students only
notes: 10-week summer placement on health-services-research projects paired with UM faculty mentors.

organization: NYU School of Global Public Health
name: William N. Rom Climate Change & Health Fellowship
deadline: Not specified - check NYU GPH fellowship page for current date

other_benefits: Training, mentoring, potential conference/publication support

flags: Duke-only; no fee

notes: Funds 8-10 fellows annually for ~300 hours of summer DH project work with mentoring and group development sessions, ending in an October showcase.

organization: Cornell University, Society for the Humanities / Digital CoLab
name: Summer Graduate Fellowship in Digital Humanities
other_benefits: Workshops, cohort community
eligibility: Current Cornell PhD students in the humanities or closely related fields who will remain enrolled the following academic year. Grad-student-only.

eligibility: Emerging and seasoned preservation professionals AND students enrolled at least part-time in a preservation-related graduate (or undergraduate) degree program (historic preservation, museum studies, history, archaeology, urban planning, architecture, preservation trades). Open to non-US residents with qualifying US-focused projects. Open to grad students.
flags: No fee; open beyond grad students too (professionals qualify), but grad students explicitly eligible
notes: One-year (Aug-Aug) leadership-development fellowship centered on a mentored capstone project meant to advance historic preservation practice, with quarterly check-ins and up to two weeks of professional-development workshops.

flags: No fee; official fellowship page returned a 403 to automated fetch — verify directly via clintonfoundation.org or clintonlibrary.gov before applying
notes: Supports archival research using the Clinton Presidential Library's holdings; four fellowships awarded per calendar year across three application cycles.

name: RBS-UVA Fellowship Program
deadline: ~April 1 (annual, historically; course applications encouraged earlier as RBS courses fill fast)

other_benefits: Access to RBS's rare book/bibliography course network
eligibility: UVA undergraduate and graduate students. Grad-student-eligible.
flags: Restricted to UVA students only; no fee

name: Buchanan Burnham Summer Scholars in Public History Program
other_benefits: Possible housing
eligibility: Current graduate students with a background in museum collections, archives, or American history; students preparing to apply to graduate school may also apply. Grad and pre-grad eligible.
flags: No fee
notes: Roughly 11-week (late May-early August) public history/archives practicum at the Newport Historical Society, ~30 hrs/week; housing may be available.

name: Montana History Network Research Fellowship (Nelson Weller Fellowship)
other_benefits: Potential publication opportunity
eligibility: Enrolled in a master's or doctoral program in history or a related field at a Montana university. Grad-student-only.
flags: Restricted to Montana university students; no fee
notes: Supports 2 weeks of archival research across at least two of three partner institutions (Montana Historical Society, Montana State University, University of Montana) between May 1-Oct 31; requires a written report and consideration of an article for Montana the Magazine of Western History.

organization: Southeast Chapter of the Society of Architectural Historians (SESAH)

flags: Requires SESAH membership (a modest professional-society due, not an application fee); regional eligibility
notes: Discipline-society research fellowship supporting a thesis/dissertation research project in architectural history or historic preservation; preference to Southern architectural-history topics.

name: Filson Institute Research Fellowship

flags: No fee
notes: One-week immersive research residency at this regional historical society/archive, themed around an annual Filson Institute research topic.

name: GC Digital Fellows Program

flags: CUNY GC doctoral students only; no fee

notes: Approximately 7 fellowships awarded per cycle; administered by Blueprint Kentucky (rebranded from CEDIK).

organization: WISCIENCE / Morgridge Center for Public Service, UW-Madison
name: STEM Public Service Fellows
amount: Not specified (professional development support provided; confirm stipend directly with program)
other_benefits: n/a
eligibility: Current UW-Madison graduate students and postdocs from any STEM discipline
notes: Fellows choose a pathway: community-engaged teaching, direct service, or policy and governance.

name: Vermont Community Fellows Program
amount: $2,000 stipend for student fellows (may be supplemented)
other_benefits: n/a
eligibility: Vermont residents age 18+, including students currently enrolled in a credit-bearing graduate program (Vermont-based, or VT residents enrolled elsewhere while living in-state during the school year)
notes: Community-based oral history/local-issues fellowship; no application fee.

organization: The Humanities Institute (THI), UC Santa Cruz
name: Graduate Public Fellowships (Summer Public Fellows track)
deadline: ~March 30 annually (summer cohort; year-long and 3-quarter tracks have separate calls)
other_benefits: n/a

other_benefits: n/a
