name: Post-Baccalaureate Fellowship
deadline: Rolling with priority review (recurring annually; 2026-27 cohort begins Fall 2026)
amount: Stipend covering living expenses; benefits after first 3 months (exact dollar figure not published)
eligibility: Recent bachelor's-degree holders who have NOT yet started a PhD/MD/MS program and intend to use the fellowship to strengthen applications to graduate or medical school in aging biology/biogerontology; explicitly a prospective-grad-student bridge role, not open to current degree students.
flags: Exact stipend amount not publicly disclosed; confirm directly before relying on it for budgeting.
notes: 9-month, full-time bench-research fellowship in longevity/aging biology. No application fee identified.

name: Postbaccalaureate Fellowship Program
amount: Competitive compensation package plus benefits (exact figure not published)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree earned within the prior 3 years, not currently enrolled in a degree program, intending to apply to a PhD or MD/PhD in biological sciences, neuroscience, or biomedical sciences; international applicants welcome subject to screening.
notes: One-year, full-time research fellowship on FAU's Jupiter, FL campus preparing candidates for PhD/MD-PhD applications. No application fee identified.

name: Post-Baccalaureate Fellowship
deadline: Priority deadline ~May 4 annually; reviewed on rolling basis after (recurring each year)
amount: Stipend for up to one year, plus a moving allowance and funding to attend an AAS meeting (exact stipend figure not published)
eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents who recently completed a bachelor's degree and intend to apply to PhD programs in astronomy or a related field during the fellowship year; not open to those already admitted to a PhD program.
notes: Research-experience fellowship at NRAO sites designed specifically to strengthen astronomy PhD applications. No application fee identified.

name: Post-Baccalaureate Fellowships in the Humanities
amount: $34,000 stipend, $1,000 one-time research/professional-development allowance, medical insurance eligibility
eligibility: Recent BA graduates who have not yet begun graduate study, planning to apply to PhD/graduate programs in Byzantine Studies, Garden and Landscape Studies, or Pre-Columbian Studies.
notes: Harvard-affiliated research institute in Washington, DC; appointment runs September 2026-August 2027. No application fee identified.

organization: University of Washington Computational Neuroscience Center / Allen Institute
name: Shanahan Undergraduate and Postbac Fellowships
deadline: Rolling; priority consideration for applications received by ~June 26 annually
amount: Paid fellowship position (exact stipend figure not published)
eligibility: Recent bachelor's graduates (pre-doctoral researchers) intending to apply to PhD programs at the interface of data science and neuroscience; mentored by current Shanahan Fellows ahead of doctoral applications.
notes: Joint UW/Allen Institute program in computational neuroscience; distinct from the separate Shanahan postdoctoral fellowship (which requires a completed PhD and is excluded here).

name: American Physical Society Bridge Program (APS)
amount: Funding set by host institution, typically comparable to standard graduate stipends; some sites add supplemental support (e.g., a Google Bridge Fellowship worth $25,000/year for 2 years at CSU Long Beach)
eligibility: Students who have NOT yet received a PhD-program acceptance letter (post-bachelor's applicants for a bridge master's, or post-master's applicants for a bridge PhD slot) intending doctoral study in physics; must be US citizen, permanent resident, or DACA recipient.
flags: No centralized funding from APS itself; award value depends entirely on the host institution.
notes: Places students into funded 'bridge' positions at partner physics departments nationwide specifically to prepare them for later PhD admission.

name: Fisk-Vanderbilt Master's-to-PhD Bridge Program
deadline: Rolling; apply via the Fisk graduate master's application (check site for current cycle)
amount: ~$2,200/month stipend, tuition and fee waiver, medical insurance, and a laptop
eligibility: Bachelor's-degree holders, especially from groups underrepresented in STEM, who are not yet fully prepared for direct PhD admission; bridges into a PhD in astronomy, biology, chemistry, materials science, or physics via a funded Fisk master's degree.
notes: Students complete a master's at Fisk before transitioning to a PhD at Vanderbilt or another partner institution.

organization: Roberta Buffett Institute for Global Affairs, Northwestern University
name: Buffett Post-Baccalaureate Fellowship Program
amount: Paid compensation plus benefits, transportation support, and local-language study funding (exact figure varies by individual fellowship placement; not published centrally)
eligibility: Northwestern (Evanston) seniors graduating in the fellowship's cycle, or alumni who graduated within the past year, committing full-time (no concurrent grad coursework) to a year working abroad in arts, human rights, community development, or global health as a bridge before pursuing graduate study or a related career.
flags: Restricted to Northwestern Evanston undergraduates/recent alumni only.
notes: One-year overseas placements with partner organizations; explicitly framed by the Institute as preparation for future graduate study or global-affairs careers. No application fee identified.

name: SREB-State Doctoral Scholars Program
amount: Doctoral Award: $20,000/year for up to 3 years plus 2 years of institutional support; Dissertation Award: one-year $20,000 stipend plus $500 research allowance; tuition/fee coverage available up to 5 years
eligibility: US citizens/permanent residents (with some state-funded slots for others) who are entering or currently enrolled in a PhD program in any field at a participating SREB member-state university, from backgrounds underrepresented in doctoral education and the professoriate.
notes: Regional program spanning 16+ southern/border US states; includes career counseling, a scholar directory, and faculty-track mentoring.

organization: Institute for Recruitment of Teachers (IRT), Phillips Academy Andover
name: Institute for Recruitment of Teachers Summer Workshop and Associate Program (IRT)
deadline: March 1, 11:59pm ET (recurring annually; 2026/27 cohort currently open)
amount: Free to participants; paid 4-week residential Summer Workshop stipend for interns, plus application fee waivers to 10-12 graduate programs
eligibility: College juniors, seniors, recent graduates, and working professionals - especially BIPOC and first-generation students - who are preparing to apply to graduate school in the humanities, social sciences, or education.
notes: Nonprofit pipeline program combining a paid summer graduate-level curriculum with intensive graduate-school application counseling and a Graduate School Kickoff Weekend; no cost to participants.
location: Andover, Massachusetts (Summer Workshop); counseling program is largely remote

name: University of California President's Pre-Professoriate Fellowship (UC-HSI Doctoral Diversity Initiative)
deadline: Varies by UC campus, typically early February (recurring annually)
amount: $37,000 stipend, California resident tuition and fees, plus a $10,000 professional-development grant
eligibility: Current PhD students in any discipline at a University of California campus, with priority for students from California Hispanic-Serving Institutions and groups underrepresented in the professoriate (Chicanx/Latinx, Black, Native American, Filipinx, Pacific Islander students; women in STEM; Asian Americans in humanities/social sciences).
notes: Nomination process and exact deadline vary by UC campus; contact your campus graduate division.

organization: Clean Energy Institute, University of Washington
name: Clean Energy Institute Graduate Fellowship (CEI)
amount: One to three quarters of salary plus tuition support (exact dollar figure not published)
eligibility: Current University of Washington PhD students (must have begun doctoral study roughly 1-3 years prior and already have a faculty advisor) conducting research in a CEI clean-energy focus area; incoming first-year students are not eligible.
notes: Especially seeks applicants pivoting to apply AI/ML tools to clean-energy research problems.

organization: Loyola University Chicago, Center for Catholic Intellectual Heritage
name: Michael J. Garanzini, S.J. Fellowships in the Catholic Intellectual Tradition
deadline: Annual, ~March 24 (2026 cycle: March 24, 2026, 11:59pm CT); recurring every year
amount: Not specified on program page (dissertation/MFA-year support stipend; confirm current figure with CCIH)
other_benefits: Career mentoring, cohort Zoom meetings
eligibility: Current graduate students enrolled in any U.S. doctoral or MFA program who have completed pre-dissertation requirements and general exams; open to students at any university, not just Loyola
flags: No application fee
notes: Work must prominently engage the Catholic intellectual tradition, any discipline. Requires 2 Zoom meetings, final report, 1-year follow-up report.

name: Association for Jewish Studies Dissertation Completion Fellowship (AJS)

other_benefits: Complimentary registration to AJS Annual Conference
eligibility: Current ABD PhD candidates completing a dissertation in Jewish Studies, current AJS members, able to defend within approximately 8 months of the award
flags: Deadline for the cycle described above has passed; recurring annual program, contact aweiss@associationforjewishstudies.org for next cycle
notes: Applicants submit CV, proposal, two dissertation chapters, timeline, bibliography, 2 letters, and department confirmation of ABD status.

name: Fein & Lapidus Fellowship
deadline: Annual, March 31 (2026 cycle closed; next cycle expected ~March 2027, notifications by April 30)

organization: Parr Center for Ethics, UNC-Chapel Hill
name: Graduate Fellowship Program

amount: Not specified (interdisciplinary cohort program; confirm any stipend with the Center)

eligibility: Current UNC-Chapel Hill graduate students in any discipline interested in ethics
flags: No application fee; UNC-only eligibility
notes: Fellows judge/moderate the NC and National High School Ethics Bowl and write one Ethics Bowl case.

name: Sadler Scholars Program

other_benefits: Work-in-progress talks, career development and publication workshops
eligibility: Current advanced doctoral students in any field with a career focus on bioethics research and education; program prioritizes candidates from groups underrepresented in bioethics
flags: No application fee
notes: Named for Hastings Center trustee Richard B. Saddler; aims to diversify the bioethics field.

organization: de Nicola Center for Ethics and Culture, University of Notre Dame

eligibility: Current University of Chicago PhD candidates graduating in religious ethics or theology, with demonstrated interest in religion/ethics/medicine intersection
flags: University of Chicago-only eligibility; limited public application detail, contact program directly

organization: Villa Albertine / French Embassy in the US (Chateaubriand Fellowship)

organization: International Mathematical Union (IMU) / Friends of IMU

Candidates must be nominated by a professional mathematician (no self-applications). Women strongly encouraged.
notes: Funded by donations from Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics winners. Covers tuition, travel, housing, living expenses. Apply via grants.mathunion.org. No fee.
location: Host developing country of the student's PhD program

notes: Grants renewable annually. Fellows commit to returning to their home country/region. No application fee. Program has funded 1,000+ fellows since 2004.

organization: Consortium for Advanced Research Training in Africa (CARTA)

amount: Stipend for 28 months plus research funds up to US$10,500, plus training and a laptop
eligibility: Holders of a Master's degree who are teaching/research staff at a CARTA partner African institution and intend to pursue (or have just begun) PhD research in public/population health; prior PhD admission is not required at application — it must be secured within the first 12 months of the fellowship. Men under 40, women under 45.
notes: 22 fellowships awarded in the 2026 round. Multi-disciplinary but focused on public/population health research relevant to Africa. No application fee.
duration: 28 months (fellowship), 4 years typical for full PhD

organization: Fondation Philippe Wiener - Maurice Anspach (Université libre de Bruxelles)

organization: Kobe College Corporation (KCC) / Japan Education Exchange
name: Kobe College Corporation Japan Education Exchange Graduate Fellowship Program (KCC)
deadline: Typically mid-March annually (check site for exact current-cycle date)
eligibility: US citizen PhD candidates who have completed qualifying exams and advanced to candidacy, with research-level Japanese language competency, planning to conduct dissertation research or study in Japan.
notes: Supports future American educators who will teach about Japan; preference for documented interest in Japanese arts, culture, education, language, history, journalism, business, or science. No application fee.

organization: Federation of European Biochemical Societies (FEBS) / PABMB

eligibility: PhD students officially enrolled in a PhD program in a Latin American country and affiliated with PABMB (via their national biochemistry/molecular biology society).
notes: Funds 3-6 month research visits to a host lab in a FEBS member country as part of the student's PhD thesis work. No application fee.
location: Host lab in a FEBS member country (Europe)

name: World Bank Group Africa Fellowship Program

amount: Consultant fees plus round-trip economy airfare to Washington, DC or a WBG country office (amount varies by placement)
eligibility: Sub-Saharan Africa nationals under 32, enrolled in the final year of a PhD program OR who completed a PhD within the last 3 years. Strong quantitative/analytical skills required; women strongly encouraged.
notes: Six-month operational placement at World Bank Group headquarters or a country office. Explicitly open to current final-year PhD students, not just post-PhD candidates. No application fee.
location: Washington, DC or WBG country offices

organization: Global Business School Network (GBSN) / Deutsche Post DHL Group
name: DHL GoTrade GBSN Fellowship Program

amount: Unpaid fellowship (no stipend); includes mentorship from DPDHL professionals, direct SME coaching, and a certified international-trade training curriculum
eligibility: Graduate business students (MBA/MSc/Master's/PhD) currently enrolled at a participating GBSN member business school worldwide, including US schools.

organization: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER)
name: Visiting PhD Fellowship
amount: Monthly stipend of €2,070, travel grant, and medical insurance during the stay
eligibility: Students currently enrolled in a PhD program (any country, including the US) conducting research on developing economies; other social science backgrounds welcome, though the institute is economics-focused. Early-career, female, and developing-country researchers particularly encouraged.
notes: 3-month visiting fellowship at UNU-WIDER in Helsinki, Finland; fellows produce research papers and present a seminar. No application fee.

organization: Villa Albertine / French Embassy in the US

eligibility: Prospective graduate students: US bachelor's degree holders (completed within roughly the prior 3.5 years), age 27 or younger, GPA 3.7+, entering a fully funded year of master's-level study in France.
notes: Funds up to 30 American students per year at one of 15 partner French institutions; courses offered in French or English. No application fee.

name: African Economic Research Consortium Collaborative PhD Programme (PhD Fellowships in Economics)

amount: Tuition/stipend support plus PhD thesis research grants awarded after successful proposal review at AERC's biannual research workshops (exact amount varies)
eligibility: Applicants from Francophone and Anglophone Sub-Saharan African countries who hold (or are completing) a Master's degree in economics/agricultural economics and have been admitted into one of AERC's Collaborative PhD Programme (CPP) partner universities.

name: Phillips Fund for Native American Research

organization: UC Berkeley School of Law, Center for Indigenous Law & Justice

notes: Named for Professor Philip Frickey, a leading federal Indian law scholar. Contact Berkeley Law's Center for Indigenous Law & Justice for exact deadlines. No fee.

other_benefits: Extensive alumni network at top law schools nationally

name: LGBTQIA+ Rights Fellowship
deadline: June 15 (rolling within Hofstra Law's admitted-student cycle)
amount: Up to two $7,500 stipends for LGBTQIA+-rights-related summer internships
other_benefits: N/A
eligibility: Students admitted to and enrolled in Hofstra Law (JD, a professional graduate degree), selected from the entering class for demonstrated LGBTQIA+ advocacy commitment.
flags: None
notes: Fellows have represented refugees and asylum seekers fleeing persecution on account of sexual orientation or gender identity. Apply via law.hofstra.edu/AdmittedStudents. No fee.
duration: Summer internship funding, renewable across law school years
location: Hempstead, NY, with internship placements nationally

organization: University of Toronto, School of Graduate Studies
name: Scholars-at-Risk Fellowship
amount: Up to $10,000 CAD for one year, plus a fee-waived Massey College membership option
other_benefits: N/A
eligibility: Current University of Toronto graduate students or incoming students accepted to a full-time master's or doctoral program who have been an asylum-seeker or refugee within the last 5 years, or whose studies have been impacted by changing political circumstances in their home country.
flags: International program (Canada) but directly serves displaced/refugee graduate students, matching this lane precisely.
notes: Requires proof of asylum/refugee status, financial need documentation, and demonstrated commitment to peer community support. Apply via U of T's Graduate Awards Office (graduate.awards@utoronto.ca). No fee.

organization: Georgetown University Law Center, Center for Applied Legal Studies (CALS)
name: Georgetown University Law Center, Center for Applied Legal Studies Graduate Teaching Fellowship (CALS)
amount: Full LL.M. tuition/fees + $70,000 stipend year one, $75,000 year two
other_benefits: Access to Georgetown's post-doctoral fellows program benefits
eligibility: Prospective LL.M. (graduate law degree) students: requires a JD, current state bar membership, and 2+ years of experience with immigration removal cases; fellows are enrolled as LL.M. candidates at Georgetown for the two-year term while co-teaching the asylum clinic.
flags: Prerequisite bar admission/experience makes this a narrower on-ramp into graduate (LL.M.) study rather than an open grad-student fellowship -- included because fellows are enrolled LL.M. students throughout.
notes: Fellows earn a Master of Laws (Advocacy) with distinction while representing asylum seekers in Georgetown's immigration clinic. Apply via Interfolio. No fee.

organization: Canada Excellence Research Chair (CERC) in Migration and Integration, Toronto Metropolitan University
name: Canada Excellence Research Chair Migration Graduate Student Stipends (CERC)
amount: Up to $10,000 CAD (Master's); up to $25,000 CAD (PhD Excellence Completion Stipend, final year)
other_benefits: Research training workshops, office space
eligibility: Full-time Master's students (1st/2nd year) applying to or enrolled at Toronto Metropolitan University in migration-related programs, and full-time PhD students in their final year, studying migration/migrant integration.
flags: International program (Canada) but squarely a migration-studies graduate fellowship.
notes: Recipients get office space and join CERC Migration's research training activities; students holding major external awards (SSHRC, CIHR, RGS) must decline or seek a top-up instead. No fee.
duration: One academic year (Master's) or final dissertation year (PhD)

name: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS)
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Women who are citizens of a country other than the US or Canada, currently enrolled (or accepted) full-time in a graduate degree program at an accredited college/university in the US or Canada, with at least one full year of study remaining; must plan to return to her home country. US/Canada citizens and permanent residents are NOT eligible.
flags: Requires connecting with a local P.E.O. chapter to submit; not a direct online-only application.
notes: Distinct from the P.E.O. Scholar Award (below); this fund specifically serves international women pursuing graduate study in the US/Canada. Application is coordinated through a local P.E.O. chapter contact, but there is no fee to apply.
location: US/Canada institutions; applicant must be a non-US/Canada citizen

name: DKG World Fellowship
deadline: ~December 1 (annual, recurring; confirm exact date each cycle)
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Women educators from outside the US and Canada (US/Canada citizens and permanent residents are ineligible) who are enrolled or planning to enroll full-time in a graduate degree program at a US or Canada university during the award year. Applicants must NOT be a current member of Delta Kappa Gamma.
flags: Restricted to international (non-US/Canada) women educators; current DKG members ineligible.
notes: Since 1960 has funded 580+ women from 100+ countries to pursue graduate study; run by an international honor society for women educators.
location: Study must occur at a US or Canada institution

organization: Educational Foundation for Women in Accounting (EFWA)
name: Educational Foundation for Women in Accounting Graduate Scholarship (EFWA)
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Women pursuing a master's-level advanced/business graduate degree with a concentration in accounting at an AACSB-accredited institution; US citizens; must demonstrate financial need. No AFWA/EFWA membership required to apply.
notes: EFWA also separately offers PhD-level ('Laurels Fund') scholarships for women in doctoral accounting programs at www.efwa.org/scholarships_postgraduate.php — check that page if pursuing a doctorate rather than a master's.

organization: Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, Schlesinger Library, Harvard University
name: Schlesinger Library Dissertation Support Grant
opens: ~Fall (application portal opens in advance of the January deadline)
other_benefits: Access to Schlesinger Library archives and staff support
eligibility: Doctoral candidates (any field) who have advanced to candidacy with an approved dissertation topic requiring use of the Schlesinger Library's women's history collections. International doctoral candidates with appropriate visa/status may apply.
notes: Supports dissertation research using one of the largest women's history archives in the US; no application fee.
location: Research conducted at Schlesinger Library, Cambridge, MA

organization: Sallie Bingham Center for Women's History and Culture, Duke University Libraries
name: Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick Travel Grant
opens: Rolling call for applications; check Rubenstein Library grants page for current cycle
deadline: Rolling/annual; confirm current-cycle date on Rubenstein Library grants page
amount: Travel/research grant (amount varies by cycle; contact library for current figure)
other_benefits: Access to a unique LGBTQ+/queer-theory archival collection
eligibility: Current graduate students (and others at any academic stage) proposing research using the Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick Papers, a foundational queer theory collection, for a dissertation, publication, or related project. Applicants must live more than 100 miles from Durham, NC, and may not be current Duke students/employees.
flags: Excludes current Duke-affiliated applicants; open regardless of academic status but grad students are explicitly eligible.
notes: Named for pioneering queer theorist Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick; funds research using her personal papers held at Duke.
location: Research conducted at Duke University's Rubenstein Library, Durham, NC

organization: CLAGS: The Center for LGBTQ Studies, CUNY Graduate Center
name: CLAGS Fellowship Award
opens: Announced annually; check CLAGS page for current call
deadline: Varies annually; confirm on CLAGS fellowships page (contact clagsfellowships@gmail.com)
amount: Research/writing support stipend (amount varies by award year — contact CLAGS for current figure)
other_benefits: Recognition within the LGBTQ studies scholarly community
eligibility: Graduate students, academics, or independent scholars working on a dissertation or book manuscript contributing to LGBTQ studies. Open to current PhD candidates at any accredited institution, not just CUNY.
notes: CUNY's Center for LGBTQ Studies also administers the CUNY-specific Monette-Horwitz Dissertation Prize for the best CUNY LGBTQ-studies dissertation.
location: Open to scholars anywhere; hosted at CUNY Graduate Center, NYC

name: Gamma Mu Foundation LGBTQ+ Graduate Student Scholarship
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Graduate and professional students of all LGBTQ+ identities, under age 35, US citizens who completed high school/GED, admitted to or enrolled full-time at an accredited US institution or program.
flags: Age cap of 35; US citizens only.
notes: Also runs a separate 'Gay Male Graduate Student' category; awards funds directly to the institution.

organization: Program in Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Studies, Yale University
name: Yale LGBT Studies Research Fellowship
other_benefits: Access to Yale's LGBT studies faculty and archival collections
eligibility: Scholars in any field, including graduate students conducting dissertation research, pursuing research in LGBTQ studies using Yale's library, archival, and faculty resources. Applicants residing within 100 miles of New Haven are ineligible.
flags: Geographic exclusion for those within 100 miles of New Haven.
notes: Open internationally; graduate students explicitly named as eligible alongside faculty and independent scholars.
location: In residence at Yale University, New Haven, CT

organization: Program in Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Studies, Yale University
name: Sarah Pettit Doctoral Fellowship in Lesbian Studies
amount: Stipend plus travel funding and room/board for a workshop week (specific dollar figure not published)
other_benefits: Mentorship and peer cohort of lesbian-studies doctoral researchers
eligibility: Doctoral candidates who are ABD (completed coursework, qualifying exams, and dissertation prospectus) working on a dissertation related to lesbian studies. Open to students from any institution/country (international students should seek supplemental funding). Yale doctoral students are NOT eligible.
flags: Yale's own doctoral students are excluded from applying.
notes: Small cohort workshop-fellowship specifically for lesbian-studies dissertation research.
location: Workshop held at Yale University, New Haven, CT

organization: APA Division 44 (Society for the Psychology of Sexual Orientation and Gender Diversity)
name: Malyon-Smith Scholarship Research Award
opens: Rolling annual call; check Division 44 awards page
deadline: Annual; confirm current-cycle date on Division 44 awards page (contact div44awards@gmail.com)
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Graduate students currently enrolled full-time in a psychology graduate program conducting research on sexual orientation and gender identity. Students in allied fields (social work, sociology, etc.) are not currently eligible. No Division 44 membership required.
flags: Restricted to psychology graduate programs specifically.
notes: Honors research into psychological issues affecting gay, lesbian, and bisexual individuals/communities.

name: National LGBTQ+ Bar Law School Scholarship
other_benefits: None beyond the monetary award
eligibility: Current or incoming law students (accepted or enrolled at least half-time) at an ABA-accredited law school, including incoming 1Ls, rising 2Ls, and part-time/evening upper-level students; open to LGBTQ+ and ally students. No Bar membership fee required to apply.
notes: Selection prioritizes demonstrated dedication to achieving legal equality for LGBTQ+ people; funds can cover tuition, housing, books, and other costs.

organization: Asian Pacific Islander Queer Women & Transgender Community (APIQWTC)
name: APIQWTC Scholarship
other_benefits: Community and leadership network within APIQWTC
eligibility: Asian/Pacific Islander lesbian, bisexual, or queer women, or transgender/non-binary individuals, currently enrolled in or preparing to enter a US-based nonprofit institution's graduate program (associate's, bachelor's, and graduate programs all qualify). Cannot have received the scholarship within the past five years.
notes: Grassroots Bay Area organization supporting API queer/trans community leaders since 1987 lineage.

organization: American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS), funded by the Mellon Foundation
name: Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowships
deadline: Late October, annually (2026 cohort deadline was Oct 28, 2026)
amount: $42,000 base stipend + up to $8,000 for project costs + $2,000 external mentorship stipend
other_benefits: External mentorship, cohort convenings
eligibility: Current PhD students in humanities or interpretive social-science departments at US institutions; must not have advanced to PhD candidacy before a rolling cutoff date each cycle. Explicitly for dissertation-stage doctoral students.
flags: Well-publicized (Mellon/ACLS partnership) — less obscure than most entries on this list, included for strong post-2020 launch and clean fit
notes: Program launched in 2023 as a new Mellon/ACLS partnership. Excludes professional/applied PhDs and terminal degrees that are not a PhD (e.g., EdD, MFA).

name: US-China AI Governance PhD Fellowship
deadline: November 21, annually (2025 cycle deadline; next expected ~Nov 2026)
amount: $40,000/year stipend (at US/UK/Canada universities) + $10,000/year research fund + full tuition/fees for up to 5 years of PhD study
other_benefits: Reimbursement of up to 5 PhD application fees for shortlisted applicants; networking events
eligibility: Current graduate students or those applying to PhD programs; must be accepted into (or already enrolled in) a PhD program and work on US-China AI governance research. No geographic/nationality restriction.
notes: New fellowship from the Future of Life Institute (2024/2025 launch); explicitly welcomes prospective PhD applicants, not only current students.
location: No geographic limitation on host university

name: Chevron Energy Graduate Fellows Awards
deadline: Rolling/annual — check application page (2026-27 cycle applications had closed at time of research)
other_benefits: Mentorship from Energy Institute faculty
eligibility: Current graduate students (master's or PhD) at UT Austin conducting energy-systems research
notes: Established 2023 via a Chevron endowment gift; inaugural cohort was 2023-24. University-specific, not a national program.

organization: NIH Fogarty International Center — LAUNCH program (NPGH LEADERs consortium)
name: Fogarty LAUNCH Research Training Program (NPGH LEADERs)
amount: NIH NRSA federal stipend scale + $15,000/year research support funding
other_benefits: Mentored global-health research training, international placement
eligibility: US predoctoral and pre-professional trainees (current doctoral/health-professions students) and postdoctoral trainees, plus partner-institution trainees in low- and middle-income countries
notes: Fogarty LAUNCH is the relaunched/restructured version (~2023) of Fogarty's global health training consortia; NPGH LEADERs is one of 7 current consortia.

name: Robert F. Youngblood Investigative Fellowship
amount: Stipend provided; exact dollar amount not publicly disclosed
other_benefits: Placement with the Missouri News Network of professional newsrooms
eligibility: Current graduate students (as well as juniors/seniors) at the Missouri School of Journalism, focused on data journalism and investigative reporting
flags: Founding year not precisely confirmed — described as a 'new' fellowship in April 2026 coverage, so likely launched 2025 or 2026
notes: Endowed by Ursula Liu in memory of her husband, journalist Robert F. Youngblood, MA '15.

organization: Cornell University — Einaudi Center for International Studies
name: Global Impact Graduate Fellowships
other_benefits: Curriculum-development mentorship, presentation opportunities
eligibility: Current Cornell graduate students from any discipline with a demonstrated interest in interdisciplinary and/or international work
notes: New in 2024 — supports fellows in developing a global-studies curriculum on inequality, identity, and justice.

organization: Georgetown University — Program on Disability Studies
name: Disability Studies Learning in Practice Fellowship
deadline: Not specified for current cycle (check program page)
other_benefits: Faculty/community mentorship
eligibility: Any current Georgetown student — undergraduate, graduate, or professional; special welcome (not requirement) to students who identify as disabled
notes: Confirmed running as of the 2023 cohort ($5,000 award); appears to be a recurring annual program.

organization: Washington University in St. Louis — Olin Business School, Koch Center
name: Own-Operate-Invest Fellowship
deadline: Varies by cohort (first cohort: Jan 6; Fall 2025 cohort: April 15)
amount: Not specified (mentorship, networking, and financial support for ownership ambitions; dollar figure undisclosed)
other_benefits: Mentorship, networking, experiential learning
eligibility: Current full-time MBA students at WashU Olin Business School pursuing entrepreneurship-through-acquisition or family-business transition
notes: Launched Spring 2025 with an inaugural cohort of 5 students — newer than Olin's original 2022 MBA Entrepreneurship Fellowship.

organization: The Institute for College Access & Success (TICAS)
name: Higher Education Policy Fellowship Program
other_benefits: Federal policy exposure, networking with policymakers
eligibility: Currently enrolled graduate students (or higher-ed practitioners) with demonstrated interest in higher-education policy who attended a community college, HBCU, TCU, HSI, or other MSI
flags: Exact founding year not confirmed — active cycles verified for 2023-24 and 2024-25
notes: Aims to build a pipeline of higher-education policy leaders from underrepresented institutional backgrounds.
duration: Multi-month fellowship with in-person DC convening

name: CfJJ Fellowship
amount: Not specified (1-2 year funded fellowship position)
other_benefits: Legislative and policy-advocacy experience; can be paired with Equal Justice Works/Skadden/Soros project funding
eligibility: Third-year law students, law school graduates, or graduate students committed to juvenile-justice reform work
flags: Launch/founding year could not be confirmed from available sources — verify recency before relying on this as a strictly post-2020 program
notes: Explicitly lists current 3L/graduate students as eligible (not only post-JD graduates).

organization: Harvard University — Center for American Political Studies (CAPS)
name: Center for American Political Studies Fellows Program (CAPS)
deadline: No open application deadline — fellows are nominated by faculty each spring
amount: Not specified (research funding, RA support, conference support)
other_benefits: Mentorship, conference support
eligibility: Incoming and current Harvard graduate students across disciplines whose research focuses on American politics
flags: Selection is by faculty nomination, not open application — differs from a typical apply-yourself fellowship
notes: Launched in 2022 with an initial class of 5 fellows.
duration: Length of the student's graduate program

organization: Johns Hopkins University / The Walters Art Museum
name: Robert and Nancy Hall Graduate Curatorial Fellowship
amount: Hourly stipend for 10 hrs/week over 9 months (exact hourly rate not publicly disclosed)
other_benefits: Museum-profession training, curatorial project ownership
eligibility: Current full-time Johns Hopkins graduate students in good standing with a History of Art background; students completing their PhD before the fellowship start are ineligible
flags: Founding/launch year could not be confirmed as post-2020 from available sources — include with caution; may predate the post-2020 lane
notes: Graduate-student-only, university-museum partnership fellowship.

name: Dissertation Fellowship for Historically Underrepresented Persons in Anthropology
amount: $10,000 (nonrenewable) plus paid annual-meeting registration and travel reimbursement
other_benefits: Paid registration and travel reimbursement to the AAA Annual Meeting
eligibility: Doctoral candidates in anthropology who are members of a historically underrepresented U.S. racialized minority group (African American, Alaska Native, American Indian/Native American, Asian American, Latino/a, Chicano/a, or Pacific Islander); must be enrolled full-time, have an approved dissertation proposal, achieve candidacy before the award, and hold AAA membership.
notes: Formerly called the Minority Dissertation Award. Award recipients are expected to serve on the selection committee for the following two years.

name: Minority Fellowship Program - Doctoral Track
opens: Not specified (2026 cohort applications opened ahead of June 2026)
deadline: Annual cycle; most recent (Fall 2026-Fall 2027 cohort) closed June 8, 2026
amount: Annual stipend (amount not publicly specified on site; varies by 2, 3, or 5-year track)
other_benefits: Individual mentoring, group coaching, statistical/research support, professional development
eligibility: Racial/ethnic minority nurses (and related behavioral health professionals) enrolled full-time in an accredited doctoral program (PhD or DNP) with a focus on psychiatric mental health and/or substance misuse care.
notes: SAMHSA-funded; part of a broader Minority Fellowship Program network administered through emfp.org that also covers master's-level tracks and other disciplines (social work, psychology, counseling).
duration: Two to five years depending on track
location: Any accredited U.S. doctoral nursing program

name: Racial and Social Justice Fellowships
other_benefits: Not specified
eligibility: Second-year (2L) J.D. students at Columbia Law School who intend to pursue careers in racial justice, or 2L students of color pursuing careers in social justice.
notes: Funds are intended to support students during their third year of law school as they prepare for racial/social justice legal careers.
location: Columbia Law School, New York, NY

name: Diversity Fellowship Program (DFP) - Fall Cycle
deadline: Late October, annually (recent cycle: Oct 26, 2025; next cycle expected ~Oct 2026)
other_benefits: Not specified
eligibility: Undergraduate seniors, recent graduates, or individuals in terminal MA programs who are applying to political science PhD programs; APSA especially encourages African American, Asian Pacific American, Latino/a, American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and MENA-descent applicants; must be US citizen/national/permanent resident or DACA recipient.
notes: For PROSPECTIVE PhD applicants (not yet enrolled); a companion 1st/2nd-year cycle exists for students already admitted to PhD programs. 12-14 fellowships awarded per cycle.
location: Any U.S. political science PhD program

name: Eugene Cota-Robles Fellowship
opens: Not specified (concurrent with PhD admissions cycle)
deadline: April 15, annually (2026 cycle closed; next cycle expected ~April 2027)
amount: $42,000 stipend (Year 1) plus student fees/NRST and an $8,000 professional development stipend
other_benefits: Professional development funding
eligibility: Newly admitted, first-year PhD applicants at UC Irvine (not current students) who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or AB540-eligible, show commitment to research benefiting underrepresented communities, and are nominated by their department.
notes: UC-system-wide diversity fellowship named for Eugene Cota-Robles, an early Mexican-American UC professor; parallel Cota-Robles programs exist at other UC campuses (Davis, Merced, Berkeley, UCSF, etc.) with campus-specific stipends.
location: UC Irvine (or other UC campuses under campus-specific versions)

name: Sloan Indigenous Graduate Partnership (SIGP)
amount: M.S.: $22,000 over 2 years; PhD: $44,000 over 4 years
other_benefits: Mentorship network, professional development
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents (or individuals recognized under the 1794 Jay Treaty) admitted to a residential master's or PhD program at an SIGP partner institution in a STEM field (including traditional-ecological-knowledge-focused programs); designed for Indigenous/Native American graduate students.
notes: Funded through the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation; integrates Indigenous perspectives with STEM graduate training and mentorship networks.
location: SIGP partner institutions (contact program for current list)

name: WMU-GEP (Graduate Education and the Professoriate) Fellowship
amount: $18,202 annual stipend plus tuition for up to 24 credits/year
other_benefits: Full tuition for program-approved courses
eligibility: U.S. citizens admitted to a WMU doctoral program in STEM or SBE (social/behavioral sciences/economics) fields; program specifically recruits students of African American, Hispanic, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander, or Native American heritage.
notes: Renewable for up to four additional years based on progress; personal statement addresses experiences with race/diversity.
duration: One year, renewable up to 5 years total

name: McKnight Doctoral Fellowship Program
amount: Up to $14,000/year for up to 3 years
other_benefits: Not specified
eligibility: African American or Hispanic U.S. citizens holding at least a bachelor's degree who are NOT currently enrolled in a doctoral program (i.e., prospective PhD applicants) and who gain admission to a participating Florida PhD program by Feb 28; covers Arts & Sciences, Business, Engineering, Health Sciences, Nursing, or Visual/Performing Arts PhDs (professional doctorates like JD/MD/DNP excluded).
notes: Statewide Florida program; explicitly for prospective (not-yet-enrolled) PhD students, fitting the pre-grad-school pipeline audience.

organization: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) — Retirement and Disability Research Consortium (RDRC), funded by SSA
name: Graduate Fellow, Retirement and Disability Policy Research
deadline: Not specified; check NBER posting for current cycle
amount: Stipend amount not published on the page; funded via SSA cooperative agreement — confirm current figure with NBER
other_benefits: Access to RDRC/NBER research network and conferences.
eligibility: Open to current PhD students (any relevant discipline — economics, public policy, sociology, etc.) conducting independent dissertation-related research on the health, labor, behavioral, or economic/policy aspects of Social Security retirement and disability programs, working under a dissertation advisor. Women, underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities, and veterans are explicitly encouraged to apply.
notes: Disability-studies-adjacent (SSDI/SSI policy research), not restricted to applicants who are themselves disabled.
location: USA (research conducted at student's home institution)

name: Graduate Fellowship Fund (GFF)
amount: Varies year to year based on endowment income; not a fixed published figure
eligibility: Open to deaf or hard-of-hearing students (Gallaudet graduates or other accredited institutions) who have been accepted into a terminal degree graduate program at a college/university for hearing students. Explicitly for prospective/incoming and current graduate students.

name: Public Policy and Civic Engagement Fellowship (National Leadership Program)
deadline: Check current cohort dates on RespectAbility site
other_benefits: Job coaching, skills development, networking, assistive technology and personal care support as needed.
eligibility: Open to college AND graduate students with disabilities, as well as people transitioning into or back into the workforce; interested in government/public policy careers.

name: Center for Inclusive Policy Fellowship Program for Emerging Disability Policy Researchers (CIP)
amount: $1,000/month stipend for 12 months, plus up to $2,000 for research costs/conference sponsorship; reasonable accommodation costs covered
other_benefits: Mentoring, exposure to global disability-policy discourse.
eligibility: Open to emerging researchers with disabilities from low- and middle-income countries who have an undergraduate degree and are early in their research careers (not senior/established researchers) — current graduate students conducting disability-policy research are eligible.
notes: A parallel 'Disability Data Fellowship' track focused on quantitative data collection is also being run under the same call.

organization: SPARC Center (OSEP-funded, NC State/Texas A&M/FSU/George Mason/UCF/UNC Charlotte consortium)
name: SPARC Center Scholars Program
deadline: Check current-cycle deadline on SPARC Center site
amount: $1,000 stipend for conference travel, plus dataset access and research support
other_benefits: Statewide longitudinal dataset access, mentorship, publication/conference opportunities.
eligibility: Open to doctoral students engaged in advanced coursework or dissertation work in special education, education policy, economics, or a related field, studying the special-education workforce; not limited to the six partner universities.

name: Snowdon Trust Master's Scholarship
deadline: Check current cycle on Snowdon Trust site
amount: Up to £30,000 (up to £15,000 toward fees, up to £15,000 for living costs)
other_benefits: Disabled Leaders Network membership, mentoring, community.
eligibility: Open to national and international disabled students (must reside in the UK for the duration of study) undertaking a taught Master's or Master's by research. Highly competitive (under 2% acceptance).
flags: UK-resident-during-study requirement; verify current application window.
notes: Titled a 'Scholarship' by the funder, but functions as a structured leadership fellowship: cohort-based, includes membership in the Disabled Leaders Network (peer community, skills development), not a plain money-only award — included on that basis.

organization: Association of University Centers on Disabilities (AUCD) — LEND Network
name: Leadership Education in Neurodevelopmental and Related Disabilities (LEND) Traineeship
opens: Not specified; varies by individual LEND site (60 programs nationwide)
deadline: Varies by host university/site — apply through the local LEND program
amount: Federally-funded stipend plus tuition benefit (amount varies by site/federal allocation); self-advocate and family-member trainees receive the same stipend as graduate trainees
other_benefits: Interdisciplinary clinical/research/leadership training in neurodevelopmental disabilities.
eligibility: Open to full-time graduate students in core disciplines (e.g., psychology, social work, speech-language pathology, medicine, nursing, nutrition, etc.) at a participating university; self-advocates and family members of people with autism/related developmental disabilities are also eligible alongside grad-student trainees.
flags: Amount/deadline vary by host site — verify with the specific LEND program.
notes: Not a single program but a national network of ~60 federally funded LEND sites; applicants should search 'LEND' plus their state/university to find and apply to the specific local program.
location: USA (every state, DC, PR, USVI, Pacific Basin)

name: Public Policy Fellowship
amount: Stipend plus modest relocation expenses (exact figure not published; confirm with Foundation)
other_benefits: Intensive exposure to federal public-policy-making process.
eligibility: Open to an exemplary professional and/or a person with intellectual/developmental disabilities, or a family member of someone with IDD; commonly used as an entry point by prospective and recent graduate students pursuing disability-policy careers, though not restricted to enrolled students.
flags: Confirm current-year eligibility language directly with JPKF/AUCD before advising an applicant.
notes: Eligibility is broader than 'grad students only' but does not exclude them — include per the 'open to grad students and others' rule.

name: Behavioral Sciences Student Fellowship
other_benefits: Faculty preceptor supervision/mentorship.
eligibility: Open to undergraduate AND graduate students in the behavioral sciences (psychology, social work, sociology, anthropology, nursing, economics, vocational rehabilitation, counseling, political science, etc.) with a defined epilepsy-related research plan and a faculty preceptor.
notes: Distinct from the Foundation's larger $40,000 Behavioral Sciences research fellowship (which targets more established investigators) — this is the student-level track. Apply via ProposalCENTRAL.

organization: Office of Special Education Programs (OSEP)-funded consortium — National Center for Leadership in Intensive Intervention (NCLII)
name: NCLII Doctoral Funding
opens: Not specified; tied to doctoral admission cycles at partner universities
deadline: Varies by partner institution's doctoral admissions deadline
amount: Full tuition, stipend, and research funding (exact figures vary by partner institution; not published centrally)
other_benefits: Research training in intensive intervention for students with disabilities.
eligibility: Open to newly admitted doctoral students (no prior special-education doctoral credits) at one of 7 partner universities (Vanderbilt, SMU, UConn, UIC, Minnesota, UT Austin, VCU) who intend to work in special-education leadership/faculty roles; requires a 2-years-of-service-per-year-of-funding payback commitment.
flags: Applicant must apply for admission to the doctoral program itself, then separately secure NCLII funding via a participating faculty advisor.
notes: One of several OSEP-funded special-education doctoral leadership pipelines (others include Project SUSTAIN); included as a representative example — only one such program included here to avoid near-duplicate listings.

organization: DSSGx Munich (Munich Center for Machine Learning)
name: DSSGx Munich Fellowship
other_benefits: Fully funded (travel/visa support typically included); works on real-world social-impact data projects
eligibility: Open internationally to students from a bachelor's degree nearing completion through PhD level, with a background in data science, ML, CS, statistics, or social/natural sciences with strong analytical skills
notes: International sister program to the US DSSG fellowship network; good "lean obscure" pick for grad students seeking an international data-for-good placement.

organization: Data Science Institute, University of British Columbia
name: Data Science for Social Good (DSSG) UBC Fellowship
eligibility: Full-time graduate students at UBC Vancouver campus (written thesis-supervisor consent required; Master of Data Science students excluded); also open to UBC undergrads with 75+ credits
notes: Restricted to UBC-enrolled students, but a legitimate university-hosted, internationally-flavored (Canada) civic-data fellowship.

name: Paragon Policy Fellowship
deadline: April 30, 2026 for the Summer 2026 cohort (biannual — Summer & Fall cohorts; next application window ~Fall 2026)
amount: Not specified on public pages (part-time, structured as an experiential fellowship)
eligibility: Currently enrolled undergraduate, graduate, JD, or PhD students, or those who graduated within the past year; Project Lead track is explicitly typically filled by graduate or PhD students
flags: Amount/stipend not published — confirm compensation directly before applying
