eligibility: Current doctoral students in mathematics at US institutions (JMM: last two years of study) or US-based mathematicians for ICM
notes: Verified via ams.org July 2026; funded partly via NSF and AMS Next Generation Fund.

name: Herbert Scoville Jr. Peace Fellowship
other_benefits: Placement with a DC-based national security/arms control NGO; mentorship
eligibility: College graduates or current/prospective master's students interested in peace and security policy
audience: Recent grads and current/prospective master's students
notes: Well-regarded but far less common than PMF/Rangel/Pickering/Truman; placements at think tanks and advocacy NGOs.

name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP)
amount: Full tuition, monthly subsistence, housing, books, travel
other_benefits: Placement at partner universities across Asia-Pacific
eligibility: Nationals of ADB developing member countries pursuing postgraduate study in economics, management, development-related studies
audience: Prospective master's students from ADB developing member countries
duration: Length of master's program (up to 2 years)
notes: About 140 scholarships awarded annually; development-policy focused.

name: Chinese Language Fellowship Program (CLFP)
other_benefits: Funds a year of intensive Chinese language training, generally in China or Taiwan
eligibility: American graduate students whose work focuses on China policy issues
audience: US graduate students focused on China policy
location: China or Taiwan (fellow's choice of institution)
notes: Funded by Carnegie Corporation of New York; trains next-generation China policy scholars.

name: Eisenhower Global Scholars Program
other_benefits: One-year Master in Public Policy (Oxford Blavatnik School) or Master in International Relations (IE University Spain)
eligibility: US citizens/permanent residents, generally ages 20-30, with a strong undergraduate record
notes: Only up to 4 scholars selected annually; funds a full master's degree at Oxford or IE University.

name: Budapest Fellowship Program
other_benefits: Placement at a Budapest-based think tank, NGO, or government office; mentorship
eligibility: Junior track: current or recent master's students; Senior track: doctoral students/PhDs/early-career professionals
audience: US master's/PhD students and recent graduates
notes: Research + teaching + host-institution placement on Hungary/CEE/transatlantic policy topics.

name: McCain Institute Junior Fellowship Program
other_benefits: DC-based placement, mentorship, human rights/democracy programming
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate students interested in democracy and human rights careers
notes: Runs three cohorts per year; smaller/less-known than flagship DC fellowships.

name: Foreign Affairs Information Technology Fellowship (FAIT)
other_benefits: Two paid summer internships (domestic + overseas at a US embassy/consulate), mentoring
eligibility: US citizens with 3.2+ GPA entering a master's degree program (or undergrad juniors) in an IT-related field
audience: Prospective master's students in IT-related fields
notes: Sibling program to Rangel/Pickering but IT/tech-diplomacy focused and far less well-known.

name: Donald M. Payne International Development Graduate Fellowship Program
amount: Up to ~$104,000 in benefits over 2 years
other_benefits: Two funded internships, mentoring, professional development, path to USAID Foreign Service
eligibility: US citizens applying simultaneously to 2-year master's programs (international development, public policy, econ, etc.)
notes: USAID's analog to Pickering/Rangel; distinct agency/program, moderately well known but included since not on the exclusion list.

name: William and Kathy Hybl Democracy Studies Fellowship
other_benefits: Research mentorship at IFES
eligibility: US or international graduate student from a Rocky Mountain-region university researching democracy-building
audience: Graduate students from Rocky Mountain region universities
notes: Only one grant awarded per cycle; very obscure/regional variant of the IFES fellowship.

organization: NGO Working Group on Women, Peace and Security
name: Women, Peace and Security Policy Fellowship
amount: Unpaid (stipend not guaranteed; verify current cycle)
other_benefits: Direct policy/advocacy experience with UN Security Council WPS agenda
eligibility: Current graduate students or recent graduates (MA/MS/PhD) in gender, human rights, IR, public policy, or related fields
notes: Niche gender-and-security policy fellowship tied to UN Security Council advocacy work.

name: Energy, Climate, and Technology Policy Fellowship
amount: Stipend (varies by track); health insurance reimbursement for eligible fellows
other_benefits: Research collaboration with Belfer Center energy/climate scholars
eligibility: Predoctoral candidates and researchers in energy, climate, and technology policy
notes: Less well known than the Belfer ISP fellowship; energy/climate governance specific.

name: Harold W. Rosenthal Fellowship in International Relations
other_benefits: Placement in a congressional or executive-branch office for the summer
eligibility: Graduate students in international relations/international affairs with one year remaining in their program
area: International Relations / Congressional & Executive Branch Policy
audience: Current graduate students in international relations/affairs
location: Washington, DC and other government offices
notes: Established 1977 in memory of a Senate staffer; well-regarded among IR programs but not a top-tier ubiquitous name.

organization: George Washington University, Institute for European, Russian, and Eurasian Studies (IERES)
name: Central Asia-Azerbaijan Fellowship Program (CAAFP)
other_benefits: Research mentorship, policy-community engagement
eligibility: Young professionals/scholars (including graduate students) from Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Afghanistan, or Mongolia
audience: Regional graduate students and early-career policy professionals
location: Remote / Central Asia and Caucasus region
notes: Supported by Open Society Foundations; regionally specific and little-known outside Central Asia/Caucasus studies.

name: South Asia Program Junior Fellowship
other_benefits: Health insurance, transit benefits, close mentorship from senior South Asia security researchers
eligibility: Graduating seniors or those who completed undergrad/master's degree within the past year
notes: One of the few full-time paid think-tank fellowships focused specifically on South Asian security.

name: WITA Academy Fellowship
other_benefits: Immersion in DC trade-policy community; networking with trade professionals
eligibility: Recent undergraduates or those pursuing a graduate degree interested in international trade policy
audience: Graduate students / recent graduates interested in trade policy
notes: Small, sector-specific (trade policy) fellowship distinct from broader foreign-policy programs.

organization: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
name: Intelligence Community Centers for Academic Excellence (IC CAE) Scholars Program
other_benefits: Hiring preference for IC positions, study-abroad and language immersion opportunities
eligibility: Undergraduate (junior/senior) and graduate students at IC CAE partner institutions
audience: Graduate students at IC CAE partner universities
notes: Federally funded pipeline into IC careers; program awareness is largely limited to partner campuses.

organization: Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security (GIWPS)
name: Hillary Rodham Clinton Research Fellowship
other_benefits: Georgetown University research-fellow appointment with benefits
eligibility: In final semester of an advanced degree, or graduated with an advanced degree within the past 3 years, with a gender/WPS-related background
notes: Named for Hillary Rodham Clinton; niche gender-security policy research fellowship.

name: Demetrios G. Papademetriou Young Scholars Program
other_benefits: Research/communications training in migration policy
eligibility: Master's students and PhD candidates still enrolled, not taking courses during the term
notes: Named for MPI's founding president; open to international applicants remotely.

organization: Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs / IIE
name: Fulbright-Clinton Public Policy Fellowship
other_benefits: Direct placement inside a foreign government ministry/institution
eligibility: US citizens with a master's-level degree in a policy field OR currently enrolled in a doctoral program, plus 2+ years professional experience
audience: Master's-degree holders or current doctoral students in public policy fields
notes: A distinct, lesser-known Fulbright variant (placement inside a foreign government), separate from the standard Fulbright US Student Program.

name: Harry Middleton Fellowship
amount: Two $5,000 fellowships/year typically (more for international travel)
other_benefits: Access to LBJ Library archives and presidential-history research community
eligibility: Preference to doctoral students whose dissertation shows how history illuminates current/future policy issues (postdocs also eligible)
notes: Small, obscure governance-history fellowship at a presidential library; directly policy-relevant by design.

organization: Dwight D. Eisenhower/Clifford Roberts Graduate Fellowship Program
name: Eisenhower/Clifford Roberts Graduate Fellowship
other_benefits: Supports dissertation research using Eisenhower Presidential Library and related sources
eligibility: Doctoral students who have completed coursework and are preparing dissertations in history, government, economics, or international affairs
location: Abilene, KS (Eisenhower Library) and partner universities
notes: Limited to nominated candidates from partner universities (2 per school); niche but real governance-history fellowship.

name: Economic History Association Sokoloff Dissertation Fellowship
eligibility: Doctoral students with approved dissertation topics in economic history who are EHA members
audience: PhD students in economics/history working on economic history dissertations
notes: Named for Kenneth Sokoloff; learned-society fellowship, low overlap risk.

organization: Fahs-Beck Fund for Research and Experimentation (New York Community Trust / SSWR)
name: Fahs-Beck Dissertation Grants
eligibility: Graduate students researching well-being/functioning of individuals, families, or communities in US/Canada
area: Social work, sociology, psychology (family and community well-being)
notes: Administered by Society for Social Work and Research; overlaps sociology/psychology of family.

organization: Society for the Psychological Study of Social Issues (SPSSI)
name: SPSSI Social Issues Dissertation Award
eligibility: Doctoral dissertations in psychology (or social science with psychological subject matter) completed in prior year
audience: PhD students/recent graduates in psychology with socially relevant dissertations
notes: SPSSI also offers Grants-In-Aid and Clara Mayo Grants for pre-dissertation/master's research.

organization: Psi Chi, The International Honor Society in Psychology
name: Psi Chi Graduate Research Grant
opens: Rolling (portal opens ~30 days before each deadline)
other_benefits: Grant management experience
eligibility: Psi Chi member graduate students (or within 6 months of graduation)
audience: Graduate psychology students who are Psi Chi members
notes: One of ~15 Psi Chi grad funding opportunities; smaller/less-known than APA awards.

name: AP-LS Grants-in-Aid for Graduate Students
eligibility: Current graduate student Student Affiliate members of AP-LS researching psycholegal issues
notes: AP-LS also offers a separate Dissertation Award for completed dissertations.

name: M. Estellie Smith Memorial Award
other_benefits: One year free SEA membership
eligibility: Graduate students conducting dissertation fieldwork in economic anthropology/archaeology
notes: SEA also offers the Halperin Award for pre-dissertation research; small learned-society grant.

name: ISPP Best Dissertation Award
other_benefits: Recognition at ISPP Annual Meeting
eligibility: Completed and successfully defended PhD dissertations in political psychology (any home discipline); nominee must be ISPP member
audience: Recent PhD graduates in political psychology (dissertation completed within prior year)
notes: Award for completed work rather than in-progress funding; niche interdisciplinary society.

organization: American Association for Public Opinion Research (AAPOR) / Roper Center for Public Opinion Research
name: W.E.B. Du Bois Fellowship in Support of Diversity and Inclusion
other_benefits: Complimentary AAPOR membership, weekly mentoring conversations with polling leaders
eligibility: Graduate students at U.S. institutions who identify as an underrepresented racial/ethnic minority in polling research
audience: Graduate students from underrepresented groups interested in public opinion research
notes: Joint Roper Center/AAPOR program launched 2023; niche and underused in general databases.

name: NCFR Olson Grant: Bridging Research, Theory, and Practice
eligibility: NCFR members, including doctoral students nearing dissertation completion
audience: Doctoral students in family science/sociology near dissertation completion
notes: Faculty/postdocs also eligible; open to late-stage doctoral students.

name: GSA Behavioral and Social Sciences Section Student Research Dissertation Award
other_benefits: Recognition at GSA Annual Scientific Meeting
eligibility: Graduate student GSA members conducting dissertation research on aging
audience: PhD students researching aging and the life course
notes: GSA also administers the Hartford Doctoral Fellows in Geriatric Social Work Program (larger $50,000 award; see separate entry).

organization: Council for European Studies (CES) / Society for the Anthropology of Europe
name: SAE-CES Pre-Dissertation Research Fellowship
other_benefits: Travel support and registration waiver for International Conference of Europeanists
eligibility: Graduate students in early, exploratory stage of European-focused anthropology/social science research (pre-coursework completion)
notes: Joint program between CES and the Society for the Anthropology of Europe (SAE).

name: Barbara Rosenblum Dissertation Scholarship
eligibility: Doctoral students conducting dissertation research on women/gender in sociology, anthropology, or related fields
notes: SWS also offers Esther Ngan-ling Chow and Mareyjoyce Green scholarships and caucus-specific awards.

organization: Carrie Chapman Catt Center for Women and Politics, Iowa State University
name: Carrie Chapman Catt Prize for Research on Women and Politics
eligibility: Scholars at any level, including graduate students, researching gender and politics
audience: Graduate students and scholars researching women/gender in politics
notes: University-center prize; small but real, funded through private donations.

organization: American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT) Research and Education Foundation
name: AAMFT Foundation Dissertation Completion Fellowship
eligibility: Doctoral students at dissertation stage researching couple/family therapy
area: Marriage and family therapy, family psychology
audience: PhD students in family therapy/family psychology
notes: Foundation also offers a Minority Scholarship for Dissertation Research ($2,000) and a Graduate Student Research Award.

organization: Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies (ABCT)
name: ABCT Graduate Student Research Grant (GSRG)
eligibility: ABCT student members with dissertation/master's research relevant to cognitive-behavioral therapy
notes: Priority given to master's and dissertation projects.

name: Pre-Doctoral Fellowship for PhD Students in Aging and Health Research
amount: $26,352 stipend (12 months) plus tuition support and travel funds
other_benefits: Carrel space/computer facilities at NBER Cambridge office, mentoring from NIA-funded network
eligibility: US citizens/permanent residents enrolled as PhD students in the greater Boston area (or willing to relocate) studying health economics/aging
audience: PhD students in economics focused on aging/health
notes: Funded by NIA; geographically restricted to Boston-area residency, which limits applicant pool/overlap.

name: ASC Emerging Scholars Award
eligibility: Graduate students in their dissertation year researching criminology/criminal justice
area: Criminology, criminal justice, sociology of crime
notes: ASC also offers division-level awards (e.g., Pamela K. Lattimore/RTI International Dissertation Award, $3,000, for sentencing/corrections topics).

name: NWSA Graduate Scholarship
eligibility: NWSA individual members engaged in master's thesis or PhD dissertation research/writing in women's, gender, and sexuality studies
area: Women's, gender, and sexuality studies (sociology/psychology/political science of gender)
audience: Master's and PhD students in gender/sexuality studies
notes: NWSA also offers Lesbian Caucus and Women of Color caucus-specific research awards.

name: Rose Laub Coser Dissertation Proposal Award
eligibility: Graduate students with an outstanding doctoral dissertation proposal on family or gender and society, approved within prior two years
area: Sociology of family, gender and society
audience: PhD students proposing dissertations on family/gender
notes: Small regional-society award named for sociologist Rose Laub Coser.

organization: Association for Public Policy Analysis and Management (APPAM)
name: APPAM PhD Dissertation Award
other_benefits: Poster display at APPAM fall conference
eligibility: Best PhD dissertation in public policy/management from an APPAM-member institution's program
area: Public policy, public management (political science/economics adjacent)
audience: Recent PhD graduates in public policy analysis and management
notes: Recognition award for a completed dissertation rather than a funding grant.

name: SPA Dissertation Grant
eligibility: SPA members with approved dissertation proposals in personality assessment
notes: Small society grant; also offers a broader Student Research Grant (up to $500, open to undergrads too).

organization: American Psychological Association (APA), Division 38 (Society for Health Psychology)
name: APA Division 38 Graduate Student Health Psychology Research Award
eligibility: Graduate students conducting health psychology research
notes: Division-level APA award, less visible than main APA Dissertation Research Award.

name: Dissertation Research Grant in Developmental Psychology
eligibility: APA/Division 7 graduate student members within one year of defending dissertation proposal, developmental psychology topic
notes: Small, division-specific; distinct from Division 7's separate Dissertation Award for completed work.

name: NCFR Darling Family Life Education Research Initiative Grant
eligibility: NCFR members, including doctoral students nearing dissertation completion, in Family Life Education
audience: Doctoral students in family life education/family science
notes: Distinct from the annual NCFR Olson Grant; awarded every other year.

organization: American Real Estate and Urban Economics Association (AREUEA)
name: AREUEA Real Estate and Urban Economics Dissertation Fellowship
eligibility: PhD students researching real estate, housing, or urban economics
audience: PhD students in urban/real estate economics
notes: AREUEA also runs a Junior Scholar/Pipeline mentoring program alongside its award competitions.

name: IARR Graduate Student Research Grant
eligibility: Graduate students researching personal relationships
notes: IARR also gives a Dissertation Award recognizing outstanding completed dissertations in relationship science.

name: APA Dissertation Research Award
eligibility: APA graduate student members with dissertation proposals approved but not yet defended, at accredited US/Canadian institutions
audience: PhD students in psychology at the dissertation stage
notes: Broader/less-specialized than division-level APA awards listed separately in this set.

organization: Society for Historians of American Foreign Relations (SHAFR)
name: Marilyn Blatt Young Dissertation Completion Fellowship
other_benefits: Announced at the SHAFR annual meeting; supports final-year writing
eligibility: PhD candidates admitted to candidacy, at the writing stage with substantial research complete; topic in U.S. foreign relations or international history, broadly defined. Must be a current SHAFR member. Doctoral candidates only.
notes: No residency requirement. Requires current SHAFR membership. One award per academic year.

organization: U.S. Army Heritage and Education Center (USAHEC)
name: General and Mrs. Matthew B. Ridgway Military History Research Grant Program
other_benefits: Supports on-site research using USAHEC's military history collections
eligibility: Individuals actively engaged in military history research, explicitly including those pursuing research as part of a master's or doctorate program in military history or a related field. Graduate students eligible.
notes: Requires on-site research at USAHEC. Recipients notified by May 1; applicants submit a financial sheet for eligible expenses.

name: ALTA Travel Fellowships
other_benefits: Support to attend and be featured at the annual ALTA conference; includes the Peter K. Jansen Memorial Travel Fellowship for an emerging translator of color or one working from an underrepresented/stateless language
eligibility: Emerging translators (no book-length translation published or under contract) who are current ALTA members; graduate students qualify if they meet the emerging-translator criterion.
audience: Emerging literary translators, including graduate students
notes: Conference attendance expected. Any source language into English, any genre. ALTA membership required (can join before applying).

name: Carl H. Pforzheimer, Jr. Research Grants
other_benefits: Supports archival and other research expenses in Romantic-era literature and culture
eligibility: Advanced graduate students, untenured faculty, and unaffiliated independent scholars working on Romantic-era (British Romanticism, c. 1789-1832) literature and culture. Graduate students explicitly eligible.
audience: Advanced graduate students and early-career/independent scholars
location: Applicant's chosen archives (has funded work internationally)
notes: Does not fund writing time or conference travel. Projects need not center on Keats/Shelley; welcomes race, empire, gender, class, and global Romanticisms.

organization: The Melville Society (Melville Society Cultural Project)
name: Walter E. Bezanson Archive Fellowship
amount: $1,000 stipend (plus possible discounted lodging near the library for up to two weeks)
other_benefits: Stipend may cover travel, meals, or living expenses; access to the Melville Society Archive
eligibility: Scholars undertaking research on Herman Melville at the Society's Archive; international scholars at the dissertation stage especially encouraged. Graduate (dissertation-stage) students eligible.
area: American literature / Herman Melville studies (author society)
audience: Dissertation-stage graduate students and scholars of Melville
duration: Short-term archival visit (lodging support up to ~2 weeks)
location: Melville Society Archive, New Bedford Whaling Museum Research Library, New Bedford, Massachusetts
notes: Requires on-site research in New Bedford. Opening/deadline dates not published; contact the Society or the Whaling Museum research room to confirm.

organization: American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA)
name: Samuel H. Kress Fellowship at ASCSA
other_benefits: Room and board at Loring Hall; waiver of ASCSA fees
eligibility: Advanced graduate students who have completed all PhD requirements except the dissertation, in art/archaeology of antiquity, whose project requires extended residence in Greece; applicant must have held a Regular or Student Associate Membership at ASCSA in a preceding year.
duration: Full academic year (early September to late May)
location: Athens, Greece (residency required, based at ASCSA)
notes: Prior ASCSA membership is a prerequisite. Fellows give a public research presentation and cannot hold outside employment without Director approval.

organization: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library (HMML), Saint John's University
name: Heckman Stipend
deadline: Semi-annual: March 15 (residencies July-Dec) or October 15 (residencies Jan-June)
amount: Up to $2,500 (covers travel, housing/meals at Saint John's, and up to $250 toward reproduction costs)
other_benefits: Direct access to HMML's manuscript microfilm and digital collections
eligibility: Scholars who have not yet established themselves professionally -- explicitly including graduate students -- whose research requires HMML's manuscript collections.
area: Manuscript studies (medieval and Byzantine manuscript research)
audience: Graduate students and other early-career researchers
location: Collegeville, Minnesota (residency at Saint John's University)
notes: Does not sponsor J-visas. Cannot be held with another HMML stipend; must wait at least two years between awards.

name: Ludwig Koenen Fellowship in Papyrology
other_benefits: Structured training/mentorship in papyrological methods
eligibility: Graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and untenured faculty seeking training in papyrology; SCS membership is not required to apply.
duration: Summer training fellowship (length varies by host institute)
location: Varies by year (hosted at a papyrology training program/institute)
notes: A brief project report is due within 12 months; preference to first-time recipients. Official page may block automated access; confirm details directly.

name: ASA Doctoral Dissertation Fellowship
amount: $30,000 stipend, plus up to $5,000 for tuition/fees
other_benefits: Unused tuition allowance may support travel to ASA Division meetings; supports focused dissertation completion
eligibility: Doctoral candidates at North American institutions who reasonably anticipate completing the dissertation during the fellowship year; must be ASA members; dissertation must focus on aesthetics. Recipients may not hold employment during the fellowship.
location: North America (institution must be in North America)
notes: Up to two awards annually. Cannot run concurrently with other major fellowships without ASA approval.

name: The Analysis Studentship
deadline: April (for the following award year; awarded biennially)
amount: Approximately GBP 17,375 (equal to a full-time AHRC maintenance grant)
other_benefits: Enables a full year of independent research free of teaching/employment obligations
eligibility: A promising philosopher without other means of support (no doctoral stipend, lectureship, or research fellowship); at the time of taking up the award must have completed at least 3 and no more than 5 years of full-time research; research must fall within the concerns of the journal Analysis.
audience: Advanced PhD-stage researchers without other funding
location: A university in the UK or Republic of Ireland
notes: Awarded every other year; cannot be combined with academic employment. Confirm the next cycle on the Trust's site.

organization: University of Notre Dame - Center for Philosophy of Religion
name: Visiting Graduate Fellowship
other_benefits: A year in residence at the Center; access to its scholarly community, seminars, and events in philosophy of religion
eligibility: A philosophy graduate student at another institution (not Notre Dame) working on a dissertation in philosophy of religion or Christian philosophy who would benefit from a year at the Center.
audience: PhD students (dissertation stage) at other institutions
location: University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame, IN (residential)
notes: Residential program specifically for students enrolled elsewhere. Confirm current-year availability and amount with the Center.

organization: McGill University Library (funded by the Hume Society)
name: McGill Library-Hume Society Research Travel Grant
other_benefits: Access to McGill Rare Books and Special Collections' extensive David Hume holdings, including original letters
eligibility: Available annually on a competitive basis to a graduate student, professor, or independent researcher pursuing a project related to David Hume and his era.
area: History of philosophy (David Hume / early modern)
audience: Graduate students (also open to faculty and independent researchers)
location: McGill University, Montreal, Canada (in-residence at the library)
notes: Requires travel to and work in McGill's Rare Books and Special Collections. Grad students explicitly eligible alongside senior scholars.

name: Language Legacies Grant Program
other_benefits: One-year grant period; extensions may be requested
eligibility: Open to language activists and researchers of any country, including graduate students; no enrollment-level restriction. Supports documentation and revitalization of languages in danger of disappearing.
audience: Graduate students, independent researchers, community members
notes: No residency or citizenship requirement. Confirm the current-year deadline on the ELF site as it varies.

organization: The Firebird Foundation for Anthropological Research
name: Firebird Foundation Research Grants (Collection of Oral Literature and Traditional Ecological Knowledge)
other_benefits: Funds recording equipment, travel, living costs during fieldwork, supplies, and research assistance
eligibility: Anthropologists, linguists, and other scholars, including graduate students (grad applicants submit a letter from their academic advisor). Focus on documenting threatened oral literature and traditional ecological knowledge of Indigenous societies.
audience: Graduate students, scholars, and Indigenous community researchers
notes: Open to all nationalities; no residency requirement. Applications must be in English.

organization: Whatcom Museum / University of Washington (Jacobs Research Funds)
name: The Jacobs Research Funds (JRF)
amount: Three tiers with funding limits of $3,000, $6,000, and $9,000 USD
other_benefits: Includes the affiliated Kinkade Language and Culture Fund under the same application
eligibility: Supports linguistic and anthropological research on the Indigenous peoples of the Americas; open to researchers including graduate students. Priority to Pacific Northwest research.
audience: Graduate students, scholars, and community researchers
location: Fieldwork on Indigenous languages/cultures of the Americas; priority to the Pacific Northwest
notes: Decisions usually announced by May 1. No stated residency requirement for applicants; geographic focus is on the language community.

name: FEL Grants for Endangered Languages
amount: Up to US$1,000 (smaller requests are more competitive)
eligibility: Individuals (including graduate students) undertaking endangered-language work; applicants must be current FEL members. Priority to projects revitalizing an endangered language or supporting its community use.
audience: Graduate students, researchers, and community members who are FEL members
notes: Paid FEL membership for the relevant year is the key gate; no residency/citizenship requirement. Confirm the next round's dates on the FEL/Ogmios site.

organization: Association for Slavic, East European, and Eurasian Studies (ASEEES)
name: ASEEES Dissertation Research Grant Program
other_benefits: Supports doctoral dissertation field research travel in Eastern Europe and Eurasia; includes a named History track (Alfred J. Rieber grant)
eligibility: PhD students of any citizenship currently enrolled in a US PhD program who have achieved ABD/candidacy by the start of research travel and have the language proficiency to conduct the work; must be a current ASEEES student member; one such grant per graduate career.
area: Slavic, East European and Eurasian studies (any discipline)
location: Eastern Europe and Eurasia (research abroad); applicant based at a US institution
notes: No US citizenship requirement, but must be enrolled in a US PhD program and be a current ASEEES student member.

name: Title VIII Research Scholar Program
other_benefits: Round-trip airfare, housing and living stipends, university affiliation, visa support, health/accident/evacuation insurance, and in-country logistical support
eligibility: U.S. citizen graduate students, faculty, and independent scholars (at least 18 by the deadline) conducting policy-relevant in-country research.
area: Russian, Eurasian and East European studies
audience: Graduate students, faculty, and independent scholars
location: Eastern Europe, Russia, the Caucasus, and Central Asia (up to two countries)
notes: US citizenship required. Funded by the U.S. Department of State (Title VIII); effectively succeeds IREX's older IARO grant.

organization: American Research Institute of the South Caucasus (ARISC)
name: ARISC Graduate/Postdoctoral Fellowships
other_benefits: Helps cover travel and/or living expenses in the South Caucasus; fellows gain ARISC institutional support and give a public presentation
eligibility: Graduate students enrolled in accredited degree-granting programs in the US or Canada, and early-career postdocs; must be US or Canadian citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Open to US and Canadian citizens/permanent residents. Requires a public presentation in the South Caucasus during the research stay.

name: PARC Fellowship for U.S. Scholars (U.S. Research Fellowship)
other_benefits: PARC's Ramallah office provides a home base, institutional affiliation, orientation, and introductions to Palestinian scholars, institutions, and archives
eligibility: US citizens who are doctoral students (ABD) or scholars holding a PhD; any field contributing to Palestinian studies (purely scientific research excluded).
location: Research in Palestine, Israel, Jordan, or Lebanon
notes: US citizenship required. Two-stage application (pre-proposal then full application).

organization: Association for Asian Studies (AAS) - Northeast Asia Council (NEAC)
name: Northeast Asia Council Japan Studies Grants
eligibility: American citizens and permanent US residents. Primarily for scholars, but PhD candidates are explicitly eligible for dissertation research at appropriate collections; graduate applicants submit an advisor recommendation to AAS.
audience: US citizens/permanent residents; PhD candidates and postdoctoral scholars
notes: A parallel NEAC Korean Studies Grants program (with the Korea Foundation) exists under the same council for research on Korea.

name: James R. Scobie Memorial Award
eligibility: PhD students who are current CLAH members; supports a short exploratory research trip to test the feasibility of a Latin American history dissertation topic.
audience: PhD students at the pre-dissertation/topic-scoping stage
location: Latin America; used the summer following the award
notes: Up to five grants awarded annually. CLAH membership required. Funds restricted to international travel expenses.

name: Brazilian Initiation Scholarship Award (BRASA)
other_benefits: May be combined with other funding
eligibility: Graduate students in any humanities or social science discipline; US-based students use it for an initial exploratory trip to Brazil to build contacts and start original research.
audience: Students taking their first research trip to Brazil
duration: US-based students: trip of at least 3 weeks (Brazil-based: at least 2 weeks)
notes: Open to both US-based and Brazil-based graduate students (reciprocal initial trip). Deadline not posted on the current page.

name: Digital Humanities Summer Institute Scholarships & Bursaries (DHSI)
deadline: Ray Siemens DHSI Bursaries: ~January; Sponsored DHSI Scholarships: ~March 1
amount: Bursaries: full tuition waiver plus dormitory accommodation; Scholarships: course registration cost minus a small admin fee
other_benefits: DH methods/tools training in a cohort setting; some travel bursaries available separately
eligibility: Students, including graduate students (bursaries are students-only; scholarships prioritize students); open internationally.
area: Digital humanities methods and tools training (text encoding, computing, digital scholarship)
audience: Students and early-career scholars building DH skills
